npc:agathelos-the-raging.text: Agathelos the Raging. Deep within Razorfen Kraul, Agathelos the Raging is penned among the thorned tunnels. His great size matters to the quilboar, who revere Agamaggan as their god and progenitor, and rage makes the armored boar more fearsome still. His strength and mass make him one of the most dangerous beasts beneath the southern Barrens. Agamaggan, a titanic boar, is the god and progenitor of the quilboar. Among the Razorfen tribes, a beast as large as Agathelos carries deep spiritual meaning. He stands roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard. The quilboar keep Agathelos from roaming freely through the Kraul. Several guards maintain a field in front of the short, dead-end tunnel where he is penned. Intruders who break through the barrier face a raging beast, made even bigger and more terrifying by his fury.

npc:aggem-thorncurse.text: Aggem Thorncurse. In Razorfen Kraul, Aggem Thorncurse bears the title Death's Head Prophet. He calls a boar spirit to his aid when threatened. Aggem guards part of Razorfen Kraul, where the Death's Head tribe dwells. His shamanic power lets him summon a boar spirit, reflecting the quilboar's reverence for Agamaggan.

npc:aku-mai.text: Aku'mai. At Blackfathom Deeps, Aku'mai haunts the sunken ruins of Elune's temple along the Zoram Strand. An Old God's corruption tainted the temple's sacred Moon Well, and Aku'mai rose from the waters as its servant. The Twilight's Hammer now sacrifices innocents to Aku'mai for power. Blackfathom Deeps was once a great temple of Elune, until an Old God's corruption tainted its sacred Moon Well. Aku'mai, a gargantuan hydra and servant of the Old God, rose from the waters. Now Aku'mai lairs in the submerged ruins of the night elves' fallen temple, a blight upon the Zoram Strand whose malice poisons the waters.

npc:arcanist-doan.text: Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. He serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. While the fanatical ranks of the Scarlet Crusade lean heavily on martial fury and holy fervor, Doan remained convinced that raw arcane power was essential to purging the Scourge from Lordaeron. Stationed deep inside the Athenaeum of the Monastery's library, he was entrusted as both a lorekeeper and an operational gatekeeper, safeguarding the Scarlet Key that secures crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

npc:baron-aquanis.text: Baron Aquanis. Blackfathom Deeps is where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair, and Baron Aquanis rises from its flooded Moonshrine Ruins. He appears when someone disturbs the Fathom Stone, while the Earthen Ring suspects the cult has corrupted him. The Fathom Stone lies beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who occupy them. Within the stone rests a fathom core, a device that reveals the history of nearby elemental activity when properly read. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover it. Disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

npc:baron-silverlaine.text: Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine's spirit lingers in the Great Hall above Pyrewood Village. He once ruled Silverlaine Keep, until Archmage Arugal unleashed worgen upon the region and they slaughtered him. Baron Silverlaine ruled a noble estate in the southern hills of Silverpine. His fortress guarded the surrounding lands and kept them safe. That peace ended when Archmage Arugal summoned worgen to fight the rampaging Scourge and unleashed them upon the region. The feral beasts could not be controlled. They stormed the stronghold, overwhelmed its guards, and butchered the baron. Baron Silverlaine remains bound to the keep's ancient Great Hall. His restless ghost wanders among the wrecked dining tables where he once feasted. The cursed lord attacks intruders who enter his former home.

npc:bazil-thredd.text: Bazil Thredd. In the Stormwind Stockade, Bazil Thredd leads the Defias inmates in revolt from the eastern cell block. Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant has been imprisoned there since the Stonemasons' riots. Bazil Thredd stood beside Edwin VanCleef when the Stonemasons Guild rose against Stormwind's nobility. The guild had been refused payment for rebuilding the city, and VanCleef rejected the government's appeasements and sparked open revolt. Thredd served as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. The city guard captured Thredd during the violent clashes that followed. VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall and formed the Defias Brotherhood, while Thredd was sent into the Stormwind Stockade. A prison riot has overrun the guards, opened the cells, and turned the Stockade into an armed fortress beneath the Mage Quarter. Thredd commands the imprisoned Defias bandits, insurgents, and allied cutthroats from a post in the eastern wing, guarded by an ogre named Hamhock. For years, he had stayed silent behind bars, seemingly forsaken. Now Warden Thelwater wants Thredd's head, hoping to break the rebellion's leadership before the chaos reaches the city streets.

npc:bazzalan.text: Bazzalan. Bazzalan commands the Searing Blade cult from the lava caverns beneath Orgrimmar. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he directs its work in Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Bazzalan has joined the Searing Blade cult in Ragefire Chasm. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, the satyr rogue commands the cult's field forces from winding lava caverns. He is swift and lethal with twin blades. From a volcanic ledge above the central chamber, Bazzalan oversees the cultist guards. Jergosh the Invoker conducts demonic rituals below. Like all satyrs, Bazzalan's ultimate loyalty belongs to demonic masters. He uses poison, quick strikes, and stealth against Horde scouts who venture near the cult's staging ground.

npc:blind-hunter.text: Blind Hunter. Deep within Razorfen Kraul, the Blind Hunter roosts in the sunless depths. This elusive albino bat prowls the quilboar redoubt, far from common bats near the cavern entrances. Razorfen Kraul winds through briars and dark caverns below ground. Common bats roost nearer the surface, where faint light reaches in from outside. The Blind Hunter keeps to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale hide and milky gaze may come from generations spent apart from natural sunlight. The Blind Hunter is thought to have lost most or all of its ordinary sight. Scholars and scouts believe it tracks prey through the gloom with keen hearing and echolocation. It rarely appears, hunting only now and then among the dense thickets. For cavern explorers, seeing this phantom beast is a rare encounter.

npc:bloodmage-thalnos.text: Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Who he was in life is not recorded, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he now lingers deep within the Crusade's holy grounds, hungering for vengeance. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. Whatever his past, the plague of undeath claimed him. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery, and crying out for vengeance and for more souls. Confined to the deepest corner of the monastery's courtyard tombs, Thalnos commands apparitions and shambling undead minions against anyone who disturbs his domain. His continued presence poses a bitter contradiction for the Crusade: an undead monstrosity lingering right beneath their sacred halls, embodying the very horror they swore an eternity to eradicate.

npc:bruegal-ironknuckle.text: Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle prowls the riot-torn halls of the Stormwind Stockade. The dangerous dwarf is a powerful brawler, and anyone trying to restore order may meet his fists. Bruegal Ironknuckle roams the Stormwind Stockade during its open revolt. The dangerous dwarf is known for his brutal brawling strength. Many of the city's most volatile cutthroats have seized the underground cellblocks, and Bruegal is among them. He does not stay in one cell, but prowls the riot-torn halls, ready to bash anyone trying to quell the uprising. Bruegal Ironknuckle is one of many rogues and outlaws held deep beneath Stormwind. The Defias Brotherhood and its ringleaders direct much of the revolt, while inmates like Bruegal show that the prison holds criminals from across the eastern realms. Whatever crimes brought him there, his fierce resilience makes him elusive and one of the deadliest lone inmates in the corridors.

npc:captain-greenskin.text: Captain Greenskin. In the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin readies a warship for Edwin VanCleef. The goblin pirate oversees its crew and construction for the Defias Brotherhood, preparing the ironclad juggernaut to sail against Stormwind. Captain Greenskin paces the main deck of the juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove. A seasoned goblin mariner, he was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for a warship. Captain Greenskin commands cutthroats, not stonemasons or bandits. His crew includes Mr. Smite, his fearsome tauren first mate, and Cookie, the murloc ship's cook. Together, they hold the gangplanks and upper deck, guarding the way to VanCleef's private cabin atop the bridge.

npc:charlga-razorflank.text: Charlga Razorflank. In Razorfen Kraul, Charlga Razorflank leads the Razorfen quilboar. They drove the tauren from the southern Barrens, claiming to fight in the name of their fallen god, Agamaggan. Charlga Razorflank rules from the tangled brambles of Razorfen Kraul. Her people revere her as a master geomancer, and no quilboar can match her experimental magic. She united her fractious kin into a lethal force. With primal earth and giant thorns growing from the remains of the demigod Agamaggan, Charlga reshaped the Kraul into a fortress that is hard to enter.

npc:commander-springvale.text: Commander Springvale. At Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale's spirit guards the halls where he fell. Once a devoted paladin and commander, he was slain with his men by Arugal's worgen and remains to haunt the castle. Commander Springvale led the garrison at Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Before the keep's ruin, he was an honorable paladin devoted to the Holy Light. After Lordaeron fell to the Scourge, he oversaw the fortress's security through those troubled days. Archmage Arugal summoned extraplanar worgen to strengthen Dalaran's failing ranks against the undead Scourge. The wild beasts soon escaped his control and descended on Shadowfang Keep. They slaughtered Baron Silverlaine and his entire guard. Springvale died in the halls he had sworn to protect, his service cut short. Death did not release Springvale. His ghost haunts the keep's council room with its spectral soldiers. He still wields paladin powers, including Holy Light and Hammer of Justice, against intruders.

npc:cookie.text: Cookie. Cookie tends the crew's cauldrons aboard the juggernaut deep in the Deadmines. A murloc among the Defias Brotherhood, he cooks beneath the watch of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. In the underground dry dock, he is the only entirely optional boss. Cookie cooks beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in Ironclad Cove. No human outrider or goblin engineer takes the duty; the solitary murloc does. How Cookie came to hold the position is unknown. The rest of the crew may doubt a murloc's cooking, but pirates rarely choose their meals with care. In Moonbrook's underworld, a meal is a meal. Cookie patrols the waterways and shores around the pirate flagship. He wields cooking utensils and throws acidic brews. Though apart from typical murloc tribes, he defends his cauldron with savage force, flinging caustic mixtures at intruders who enter the docks. His station lies away from the main gangplanks, so many who storm the cove pass his kitchen by. Cookie is the only overseer aboard the Defias juggernaut who can be bypassed.

npc:dark-iron-ambassador.text: Dark Iron Ambassador. Deep within Gnomeregan, the Dark Iron Ambassador draws notice as an envoy of his clan. His presence leaves the clan’s interest in the ruined gnome capital unexplained. Among Gnomeregan’s irradiated halls, the Dark Iron Ambassador represents his clan. No one explains the purpose of his mission.

npc:dextren-ward.text: Dextren Ward. In the Stormwind Stockade, Dextren Ward remains a prisoner amid a bloody uprising. Before his capture, he dug up bodies at Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood and sold them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's town council has marked him for death. Before chains bound him beneath Stormwind, Dextren Ward robbed graves in Duskwood for profit. At Raven Hill Cemetery, where sorrow and horror had grown, he dug up the newly buried dead. He sold the bodies to local practitioners of dark arts. Morbent Fel, a necromancer whose rituals plagued Duskwood and swelled the undead ranks, was Ward's main customer. By supplying him with bodies, Ward helped spread terror through Darkshire. Stormwind authorities eventually captured Ward and brought him to the Stockade. His crimes left the people of Duskwood demanding justice, and Councilman Millstipe called for Ward's hand as proof. A rebellion swept through the Stockade, and Ward was freed from his cell amid the chaos. Armed and vicious, he seized control of his corner of the prison and uses fear to keep intruders away. Alliance forces seeking to restore order count him among their priority targets.

npc:edwin-vancleef.text: Edwin VanCleef. In the Deadmines, brilliant Edwin VanCleef commands the Defias Brotherhood. He once led the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. The House of Nobles denied the workers their promised pay, and VanCleef now seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild as it rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War. A peerless craftsman and idealist, he mastered architecture and directed the building of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. His childhood friend Mathias Shaw trained him in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft, making VanCleef a deadly operative as well as a master architect. After years of labor, the Stonemasons finished rebuilding Stormwind. The House of Nobles had run up colossal debts through military campaigns and refused the guild its promised compensation. VanCleef demanded restitution, but the nobles dissolved the guild. He led the workers in a riot and out of the city. In the chaos, his lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and left in the Stockade. In Westfall, VanCleef gathered the exiled workers and allied outcasts under the Defias Brotherhood's banner.

npc:electrocutioner-6000.text: Electrocutioner 6000. In Gnomeregan's Launch Bay, Electrocutioner 6000 guards the upper platform. The spider tank fights for Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who follow him. Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who follow him took control of Gnomeregan's war machines after the city fell. Electrocutioner 6000 guards the upper platform of the Launch Bay, striking intruders with high-voltage current. Electrocutioner 6000 guards the Workshop Key, which opens Gnomeregan's back door into its workshops. Bring down the machine, and the key offers a quicker route into the city's depths.

npc:fenrus-the-devourer.text: Fenrus the Devourer. In Shadowfang Keep, Fenrus the Devourer prowls the upper sanctum. Archmage Arugal keeps the enormous worg as a pet and guardian, its body swollen by unnatural magic. Intruders seeking the archmage's study must face the beast and its master. Fenrus the Devourer lurks outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers deep within Shadowfang Keep. Unlike the worgen on the ramparts, Fenrus is a worg, swollen to enormous size. The beast prowls among the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatus in Arugal's private study. The archmage keeps Fenrus as both pet and guard against anyone who comes seeking his head. Fenrus's unnatural bulk points to dark magic saturating the keep since Baron Silverlaine's downfall. Archmage Arugal or his unleashed worgen warped the creature through arcane or shadowy experiments, turning a native predator into a ravenous juggernaut. Fenrus is so feral and bound by magic that no hunter can charm or tame him.

npc:gelihast.text: Gelihast. In Blackfathom Deeps, Gelihast guards a strange altar in the flooded Pool of Ask'ar. His Blindlight murlocs gather around him in the sunken temple. Deep beneath the Zoram Strand, Gelihast has claimed a lair in Blackfathom Deeps. Most murlocs keep to coastal shallows, but he strikes at intruders with twin swords, moving too quickly for many to react. Casters who come within his reach rarely survive. Gelihast rules the Pool of Ask'ar with his Blindlight brood, who swarm to his side at the first sign of trouble. An altar stands beyond his lair. Those who defeat him and touch it receive the Blessing of Blackfathom.

npc:ghamoo-ra-classic.text: Ghamoo-ra. In Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar. The ancient giant turtle tramples anyone who comes near. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple to Elune. Flooded now, the ruins are claimed by naga, satyr, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among them, his enormous, thick shell turning aside all but the most determined blows. Lesser turtles surround Ghamoo-ra on a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, and they leave travelers be. He alone attacks, crushing anyone who comes near beneath his trampling bulk.

npc:gilnid.text: Gilnid. Deep in the Deadmines, Gilnid runs the goblin forges for the Defias Brotherhood. Known as the Smelter, he oversees the work that turns raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. His foundry makes the heavy cannons the Brotherhood needs to strike Stormwind. Deep in the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood depends on skilled hands to forge its weapons of war. Gilnid, VanCleef's head smelter, commands goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Taller than most of his kin, he drives them through smoke and slag, barking orders and allowing no breaks. Their work turns raw iron ore into heavy plating and deadly ordnance.

npc:hamhock.text: Hamhock. In the Stormwind Stockade, Hamhock remains locked among the rioting prisoners. The massive two-headed ogre is one of the prison’s most brutal inmates. Hamhock is a towering two-headed ogre in the Stormwind Stockade. The prison was built for petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, so his size makes him an imposing presence among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control, Hamhock stayed amid the disorder, crushing anyone who entered his cellblock. No record tells how Hamhock was captured or why he was locked among Stormwind’s thieves and dissidents. Whatever brought him to the Stockade, he is now one of its most dangerous inmates.

npc:herod.text: Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause. Because Herod oversees the armaments and martial training of the Crusade's front-line warriors, taking him down is essential for anyone seeking to dismantle the order. Raleigh the Devout, an ex-Crusader disillusioned with the order's madness residing in Southshore, calls for Herod's demise to shatter their military leadership. Across Lordaeron, the dreadlord Varimathras in the Undercity similarly seeks his execution to clear out a dangerous human bastion bordering Forsaken territory.

npc:high-inquisitor-fairbanks.text: High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the bearer of the legendary Ashbringer. He stood beside the Highlord when Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien founded the Scarlet Crusade, at first a noble order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

npc:houndmaster-loksey.text: Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the hounds guarding the Library wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb. Loksey is not the only beast handler in his family serving the cause. His brother, Huntsman Leopold, serves as the Scarlet Crusade's envoy to the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel. Leopold holds a low opinion of his brother, privately asserting that Loksey can barely manage his own hounds, let alone represent the order in high-stakes diplomacy. Despite Leopold's scorn, Loksey remains a key officer within the Monastery's inner hierarchy.

npc:interrogator-vishas.text: Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

npc:jergosh-the-invoker.text: Jergosh the Invoker. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Jergosh the Invoker plots against the Horde. He leads Searing Blade cultists in Ragefire Chasm and practices demonic arts while Thrall guides the orcs toward honor and shamanism. Jergosh gathers the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. While Thrall leads the orcs toward honor and shamanism, Jergosh turns to demonic power. He hides in Ragefire Chasm, where he draws followers into a sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. From below the Horde capital, the cult works against the path the new Horde has chosen.

npc:kam-deepfury.text: Kam Deepfury. In Stormwind's Stockade, Kam Deepfury waits apart from the Defias rebels. The Dark Iron dwarf was captured after arranging the blast that shattered the Thandol Span, far to the north. Kam Deepfury is a Dark Iron dwarf held deep in the Stormwind Stockade. Most prisoners there are disgruntled Stonemasons or Defias rebels, but he belongs to neither. Captured and brought to Stormwind after an operation crippled vital northern infrastructure, he remains cut off from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain. Like the rebels who share the corridors, he is hostile to the Alliance. Alliance intelligence at Dun Modr, near the Wetlands' northern border, named Kam Deepfury as the chief architect of the blast that shattered the Thandol Span. The explosion severed one of the massive stone bridges linking the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. It crippled a vital trade and military route for Ironforge and the Alliance, and killed a kin of the dwarf commander Longbraid the Grim.

npc:lady-anacondra.text: Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession. Now styling herself Lady Anacondra, she stands guard among the first subterranean chambers of the Wailing Caverns. Like her fellow Fanglords, she abandoned the traditional tenets of the Cenarion Circle in favor of the vicious aspects of the viper. Channeling lightning, nature magic, and slumbering trances, she enforces Naralex's twisted slumber and works to spread the nightmare's corruption into the arid land above.

npc:lady-sarevess.text: Lady Sarevess. Within Blackfathom Deeps, Lady Sarevess works dark sorceries in the flooded ruins. Lady Sarevess performs rituals in a flooded grotto within the Pool of Ask'ar. The Twilight's Hammer cultists haunt the sunken temple too, pursuing their own worship deeper in the cavern. Lady Sarevess commands elemental currents and crackling lightning. Loyal naga sentinels and summoned water elementals guard her sanctuary as she fights intruders who threaten her dark work.

npc:lord-cobrahn.text: Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn is one of the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf druid of Naralex's noble order, which hoped to heal the Barrens, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Taking a lethal serpent guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before his fall, Cobrahn was one of the noble druids who followed Naralex. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Cobrahn accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Cobrahn's mind shattered alongside his brothers. Rather than channeling the traditional totemic beasts of Cenarion tradition, the nightmare warped Cobrahn's shapeshifting into something predatory and reptilian. He now commands a deadly serpentine form that he unleashes in battle. Flanked by venomous deviate pythons and bearing a vicious clawed right hand, he oversees his section of the grottos, violently purging anyone seeking to break the nightmare's hold on the caverns.

npc:lord-pythas.text: Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally one of the personal guards of the druid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before his corruption, Pythas was a seasoned night elf warrior who served among the druid Naralex's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Alongside his martial training, he took up the druidic arts in service of Naralex's dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures. When Naralex's connection to the Emerald Dream was hijacked by dark nightmares, Pythas's mind succumbed alongside those of his fellow acolytes. Abandoning his former loyalty, he became one of the leaders of the Druids of the Fang. Where his fellow serpent lords favor cunning spellcasting or beast forms, Pythas seamlessly blends lethal combat prowess with nature magic. He now prowls the winding tunnels of the caverns, determined to defend the nightmare's twisted grip on the cavern spring.

npc:lord-serpentis.text: Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness. Succumbing completely to the corruption radiating from Naralex's twisted dreams, Serpentis and his fellow druids became the Druids of the Fang. Forsaking traditional Cenarion balance and the totem animals of old, they now seek to remake the Barrens to match their own twisted dreams rather than heal it. Serpentis rules the sect as one of its four leaders, alongside Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn and Lord Pythas.

npc:lorgus-jett.text: Lorgus Jett. In Blackfathom Deeps, Lorgus Jett commands the Twilight's Hammer among flooded ruins. The Horde has marked him as a target. Lorgus Jett is a human among the Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps. While many cultists there are orcs or tauren, Jett ranges from the upper Moonshrine Ruins to the tunnels beyond Gelihast, the murloc defiler. He coordinates the cult's rituals and violent ambitions in the ancient night elf ruins.

npc:miner-johnson.text: Miner Johnson. Deep in the Deadmines, Miner Johnson wanders among the Defias laborers. He is a seasoned miner who oversees excavation ahead of the heavy machinery, though he appears only now and then. Miner Johnson works among the laborers digging beneath the Deadmines for Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress. He waits in an alcove to the left, before the shredders in the Mast Room. Stronger and more aggressive than the other miners, he can be hard to find as he wanders the tunnels. Beneath Moonbrook, the Defias Brotherhood needs ore for weapons, reinforced shafts, and mechanical contraptions. Johnson and the other miners dig the mineral seams beneath Westfall. Anyone who enters his work area will find that he guards it fiercely.

npc:mr-smite.text: Mr. Smite. At Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite keeps watch over the Defias ship and its crew. The tauren serves Captain Greenskin as first mate, guarding the docks where Edwin VanCleef's dreadnaught is being fitted out. Any intruder who meets him faces a changing array of weapons and formidable strength. Mr. Smite keeps order on the docks of Ironclad Cove as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. The Defias Brotherhood is made up mostly of disaffected humans and goblin tinkerers, yet Smite is a battle-hardened tauren far from Kalimdor's plains. He has charge of a rowdy pirate crew while they fit out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught, and he allows no disruption to the work. Mr. Smite fights with more than brute force; he is a showman and a versatile weaponmaster. He toys with challengers, drawing out the fight and offering them a false hope of victory. When pressed, he stamps the ground with such force that foes are stunned, then searches a nearby chest for another weapon. He begins with a quick dueling blade, moves to twin cleaving reavers, and brings out a huge two-handed warhammer when pushed far enough.

npc:mutanus-the-devourer.text: Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption gave that nightmare the shape of an immense, albino murloc.

npc:naralex.text: Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed to the Barrens with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom. Naralex seated himself in deep meditation deep within the subterranean caverns, but his noble design collapsed the moment his consciousness touched the realm of the Dream. Rather than finding peaceful fonts of wild nature, his mind was ensnared by a malignant, encroaching corruption—an Emerald Nightmare. The festering corruption seized the sleeping druid's body, transforming him into an open conduit through which dark energies bled into the living world. The pristine springs turned foul, sprouting mutated fungal blooms and warping the native beasts of the caverns into ravenous deviate horrors.

npc:oggleflint.text: Oggleflint. Beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint leads the trogg tribe in Ragefire Chasm. His pack climbs from lava-filled tunnels toward the surface, where he commands them near the cavern entrance and threatens the Horde capital above. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs climbed from fiery tunnels into Ragefire Chasm. They carved a primitive domain among the molten rock and defend it with brutal force. Troggs have little advanced civilization, and Oggleflint rules his pack through sheer strength. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent diplomats into the chasm to make peace with the troggs. The troggs turned on them and killed them. Maur Grimtotem, one of the envoys, lies dead in the caverns under Oggleflint’s watch. Near the cavern entrance, the chieftain waits and strikes at outsiders who venture into the dark. Oggleflint’s tribe lives directly beneath Thrall’s capital, a hazard the Horde cannot tolerate. The troggs creep closer to the surface, and their volatile nature threatens to carry them into the Drag and Cleft of Shadow if left undisturbed.

npc:old-serra-kis.text: Old Serra'kis. Beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, Old Serra'kis lurks in the flooded depths of Blackfathom Deeps. The enormous threshadon is hidden in a submerged cave, and deadly to anyone who seeks him there. The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins. Beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, dark waters conceal older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look. To reach Old Serra'kis, you must dive deep beneath the temple floor into a flooded cavern. No air pockets break the water, making the cave as deadly as the beast within. Cornered in the murk, Serra'kis shows an unnatural resilience. He drains life from his attackers with shadow energy, sustaining his own vitality in the darkness.

npc:overlord-ramtusk.text: Overlord Ramtusk. Deep in Razorfen Kraul, Overlord Ramtusk leads the quilboar warriors into battle. He cries out for victory and for Agamaggan, and his fall breaks the Kraul defenders' martial strength. Overlord Ramtusk commands the quilboar stronghold deep in Razorfen Kraul, in the southern Barrens. He enters battle with a cry to Agamaggan, the boar demigod, and rules the Kraul's fighters with unyielding authority. Ramtusk directs the quilboar warriors through the Kraul's winding brambles. He keeps tight discipline among the bristled fighters who defend their tribe's sanctum. Elite marksmen flank him as he fights on the front line, bellowing rallying shouts and unleashing slams that can break opposing battle lines in seconds.

npc:rhahk-zor.text: Rhahk'Zor. Deep in the Deadmines, Rhahk'Zor drives the work forward by force. As head foreman, he keeps Defias laborers and miners in line while they build Edwin VanCleef's underground fortress. The Defias Brotherhood has turned Moonbrook's abandoned gold mines into an underground fortress. Rhahk'Zor was appointed head foreman to coordinate the work. He oversees the excavation crews and laborers as they carve tunnels and build VanCleef's secret projects. Rhahk'Zor keeps order with muscle and an immense stone-headed hammer. Defias diggers and goblin engineers know that defiance or falling behind schedule can bring a crushing blow from the towering foreman.

npc:scarlet-commander-mograine.text: Scarlet Commander Mograine. Scarlet Commander Mograine serves as the military leader garrisoned inside the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A zealous paladin of the Scarlet Crusade, he defends the chapel alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane. Both the Horde and Alliance target him to disrupt the zealots threatening Tirisfal Glades and the surrounding lands. Stationed within the grand Crusader's Chapel at the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine commands the standing garrison of the Scarlet Crusade. He wields the holy power of a paladin with ferocious dedication, relying on retribution, divine shields, and stunning blows to shatter any whom the Crusade deems corrupted or unclean.

npc:sneed.text: Sneed. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed directs the Defias Brotherhood’s timber work. From the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to cut lumber for Edwin VanCleef’s secret juggernaut. The Defias Brotherhood draws most of its members from human stonemasons and laborers, but an ironclad warship needs skilled trades. Edwin VanCleef brought Sneed in for his engineering knowledge and ruthless efficiency. Sneed works in the Mast Room, beside the underground rail network. There he directs the felling, cutting, and shaping of timber for VanCleef’s colossal dreadnaught. Sneed cares about cutting costs and meeting quotas, whatever the consequences. He directs the work from a custom shredder fitted with oversized buzz saws. Its blades turn raw trunks into shipbuilding timber in seconds. When intruders corner him, Sneed uses the machine’s armor to grind them down. If it fails, he scrambles from the wreckage and fights barehanded.

npc:sneed-s-shredder.text: Sneed's Shredder. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed's Shredder cuts timber and guards the works. Goblin taskmaster Sneed pilots the machine for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights, turning its blades against intruders. In the Deadmines foundry, goblin shredders cut timber for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut. They also meet intruders with armored force. Sneed oversees the lumber works and pilots this modified machine himself, wielding its oversized buzzsaw as a weapon of defense. Sneed rides above the spinning blades in an open cockpit, protected by heavy iron plating. The machine's clatter can scatter his foes. When the shredder breaks down and collapses in sparks, Sneed leaps from the wreckage and fights on.

npc:taragaman-the-hungerer.text: Taragaman the Hungerer. Beneath Orgrimmar, Taragaman the Hungerer prowls the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm. The Horde seeks to destroy the hulking felguard, feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, and end the demonic taint beneath the city. Taragaman the Hungerer prowls among Ragefire Chasm's magma pools, threatening Orgrimmar below. Scouts and young warriors sent into the dark caverns see the demonic felguard as the Searing Blade cult's leader. With infernal strength, he bends the weak-willed and corrupts the passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

npc:targorr-the-dread.text: Targorr the Dread. Deep in the Stormwind Stockade, Targorr the Dread waits among the rioting convicts. His execution was delayed by corruption and neglect, and the Defias uprising gave him a chance to escape. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served Warlord Gath'Ilzogg as the Blackrock clan's supreme executioner. He worked from the occupied ruins in Redridge, where his cruelty surpassed even the Dark Horde's violent ways. Stormwind guards and militiamen who defended the borderlands suffered torment and slow deaths at his hands. Across the kingdom, few names were more reviled. After Alliance forces captured Targorr alive, they brought him in chains to the capital and locked him in the high-security Stockade. His execution stalled in Stormwind's judicial and political bureaucracy. Graft, endless paperwork, and neglect kept the courts from delivering the death sentence he had earned. A bloodthirsty war criminal remained in a cell beneath the heart of the city. When the Defias Brotherhood broke prisoners out by force, Targorr seized his chance. He escaped his cell and joined the Defias rioters, turning his cellblock into a slaughterhouse. Warden Thelwater has lost control of the prison. Lakeshire still bears the wounds Targorr dealt its defenders, and seeks adventurers willing to enter the riots and bring back the butcher's head.

npc:twilight-lord-kelris.text: Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals in worship of the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos. Within the Moonshrine Sanctum, Kelris oversees the cult's worship of Aku'mai, a vicious three-headed hydra and servant of an Old God. Allied with the naga, the Twilight's Hammer occupies the drowned temple, and Kelris presides over the cult's rites, sacrificing innocents to Aku'mai for power.

npc:verdan-the-everliving.text: Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. He dwells amid the nightmare spreading from the sleeping druid Naralex, alongside the corrupted Druids of the Fang, and violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Verdan is a hulking bog beast, an elemental of foliage, silt, and mire that lurks in the overgrown depths of the Wailing Caverns. Nothing is known of him from before the caverns fell to corruption; he is simply the largest and most dangerous creature in their lush, flooded hollows.

npc:viscous-fallout.text: Viscous Fallout. In Gnomeregan's lower passages, Viscous Fallout drifts through the toxic runoff. Radiation flooded Gnomeregan on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice, meant to wipe out the invading troggs. The fallout filled the city's lower levels with toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental of those poisoned depths, its substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Its origins before the fall are unknown. Viscous Fallout drifts through the irradiated lower passages as a living pool of toxic sludge. It spews volleys of toxin and lashes out at anything in its path. Those who enter Gnomeregan to cleanse its tainted depths must destroy the creature.

subzone:camp-narache.text: Camp Narache. Young tauren begin their training at Camp Narache, high on Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. The camp is the Hawkwind tribe’s ancestral home, where elders preserve old ways as quilboar press close and centaur scouts linger. Camp Narache sits at the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa, the main settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. Hide lodges and pavilions house the wounded, store weapons, bake bread, and offer a place for meditation and communion with ancestors. At the camp’s heart, elders and path trainers gather in a circle. Greatmother Hawkwind guides the newly initiated as they take up their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother. Steep cliffs shield Camp Narache, but threats reach the mesa all the same. Bristleback quilboar from Brambleblade Ravine press into Hawkwind lands, while centaur scouts remain in the distance. Young hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors prove their mettle by thinning aggressive wildlife, guarding the village well, and driving back quilboar raiders. Then they descend the grand path into Mulgore’s wider valleys.

subzone:coldridge-valley.text: Coldridge Valley. In Coldridge Valley, young dwarves and gnome refugees train for service to Ironforge. Snow blankets the sheltered vale in Dun Morogh's southwestern heights, and Coldridge Pass is its lone route to the wider mountain realm. Anvilmar is where new recruits learn to fight, move unseen, and wield sorcery. Veteran dwarven instructors train them alongside displaced gnome scholars. Beyond the hall, snow covers the valley floor, where boars and hungry winter wolves test the novices' skill at surviving the frontier. Sheer cliffs keep the vale apart from much of Dun Morogh's trade. Frostmane trolls camp in the valley, including at Frostmane Hovel, and skirmish with mountaineers over their ancestral claims against dwarven encroachment. Rockjaw troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass, the tunnel linking the valley to Kharanos. With the pass blocked, travelers and supplies cannot move freely between the valley and Ironforge, the mountain realm's high seat.

subzone:deathknell.text: Deathknell. Newly awakened Forsaken gather in Deathknell, a fortified village in a secluded valley of southwestern Tirisfal Glades. Mindless Scourge, Scarlet zealots, and dangerous beasts press the settlement as the undead claim a place in Sylvanas Windrunner’s kingdom. You enter Deathknell through a narrow gorge, sealed by elite Deathguards against intruders. Newly awakened undead first open their eyes here, north of the Silverpine border and behind jagged hills. Most Tirisfal settlements kept the human names they bore under the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, but the undead who claimed this town gave it a new name. The old church anchors the southern grounds, where the Forsaken hold on. North of it, the village forge and surrounding streets remain overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Local caretakers bring new arrivals into the Banshee Queen’s service. Deathknell faces danger from every side. Night Web’s Hollow, a gold mine northwest of the village, has fallen to monstrous spiders, cutting off a resource vital to the Forsaken’s fledgling economy. Southeast of town, the Scarlet Crusade keeps an encampment in the hills, watches the pass, and trades couriers with strongholds to the east while testing the valley’s defenses. Caretakers fight the mindless undead roaming the northern ruins and gather scrap metal, tools, and supplies for newly arisen souls setting out on the long road ahead.

subzone:northshire-abbey.text: Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey trains new defenders in Northshire Valley, among Elwynn Forest's northern foothills. Rebuilt after the First War, it is the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a leading school for those answering Stormwind's call. Clerics from Lordaeron came south centuries ago to spread the Holy Light and founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery soon became part of kingdom life, caring for the sick and tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. In the First War, brigands and the Orcish Horde attacked it repeatedly, and the abbey was destroyed. After the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary and refounded its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire. Northshire Abbey trains volunteers, militia recruits, and novices who hope to defend Stormwind. Its Main Hall, Hall of Arms, and Library Wing house instructors in martial, arcane, and holy arts, while scouts and rogues train in the outer yards. The Knights of the Silver Hand keep watch, but peace remains fragile. Kobolds overrun nearby mines, aggressive wolves prowl the orchards, and Defias Brotherhood agents stalk the valley roads. They steal ancient scrolls and sacred librams from the abbey's archives.

subzone:sen-jin-village.text: Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear on Durotar's southern shore. Vol'jin founded it after Zalazane drove his people from the Echo Isles, naming it for his fallen father. The villagers endure exile and prepare to reclaim their home. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear survivors on Durotar's shore. After the witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin led them across the strait to the mainland. They raised crude huts beneath coastal cliffs, facing the water and the home they had lost. The village bears the name of Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father, who was captured and sacrificed by murlocs during the Third War. Though the Darkspear are closely allied with Thrall's Horde, exile remains their burden. Each day, the lost isles lie just across the shallows. Life in Sen'jin Village turns on preparation and defense. Quilboar raids, aggressive sea beasts, and Zalazane's hexes from across the sea threaten the villagers. Herbal remedies and potent alchemical spirits help sustain them. Vol'jin coordinates the tribe's wider defense from the Horde capital, while local shamans, hunters, and scouts gather recruits arriving from the Valley of Trials. They seek resources, guard Durotar's southern flank, and plan Zalazane's downfall.

subzone:shadowglen.text: Shadowglen. Young night elves begin their training in Shadowglen, beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. The vale gathers around Aldrassil, where elders, priestesses, and mentors guide them before they travel farther into the world. Shadowglen lies beneath the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil, ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Eternal dusk falls over the vale, where Aldrassil rises as a massive barrow-tree. Its hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors who guide young night elves beginning their training. A narrow mountain pass leads south toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar. This single route out leaves the sanctuary sheltered and peaceful. Danger reaches even this sheltered vale. Shadowthread Cave lies in the extreme northwest, where venomous spiders threaten the glade. Young defenders drive back the encroaching vermin and untamed wildlife before venturing farther among Teldrassil's boughs.

subzone:valley-of-trials.text: Valley of Trials. In the Valley of Trials, young Horde recruits test their strength in southern Durotar. Orcs and Darkspear trolls face the valley’s wildlife and dangers before they leave ready to defend their people. Young fighters face the Valley of Trials before they venture into Durotar. Chieftains and trainers watch over them from The Den, a shelter carved into the cliffs. In the sunlit gulch, recruits hunt scorpids, cull aggressive boars, and keep lazy peons in line as they harvest scarce timber. The trial is hard, and only those who prove their mettle earn the right to leave as soldiers of the Horde. Those who fail are left beneath the desert sun.

topic:alliance-of-lordaeron.text: Alliance of Lordaeron. The Alliance of Lordaeron was the historic grand coalition of the seven human kingdoms, Khaz Modan dwarves, Wildhammer gryphon riders, gnomes, and high elves formed to resist the Old Horde in the Second War. Led militarily by Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and diplomatically by King Terenas Menethil II, it shattered the invading orcish forces and secured the Eastern Kingdoms. Though political fractures and the devastation of the Scourge tore it apart during the Third War, its legacy laid the foundation for the current Alliance. Following the horrific sack of Stormwind in the First War, Regent Lord Anduin Lothar brought the battered southern refugees across the Great Sea to Capital City. Pleading their cause before King Terenas Menethil II, Lothar convinced him to gather the rulers of the human nations in council. Old rivalries and border tensions ran deep, but the threat of the Horde outweighed them. Choosing Lothar as their Supreme Commander, the seven human nations bound themselves together in a desperate pact. Facing brutal orcish warriors, dark warlocks, and monstrous red dragons, the Alliance forged entirely new doctrines of war. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Lothar established the Knights of the Silver Hand, elevating holy paladins like Uther the Lightbringer to counter the Horde's dark magic. When the war raged across the Hinterlands and quelled the siege of Aerie Peak, Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his fierce gryphon riders to rule the skies. Shortly thereafter, the Bronzebeard dwarves and Gnomeregan gnomes were liberated, joining high elven rangers under Alleria Windrunner. Despite the treacherous betrayal of King Perenolde of Alterac, the grand coalition drove the Horde back to Blackrock Spire and crushed their dominion. Victory brought bitterness rather than enduring peace. Bitter disputes erupted over the high taxes required to maintain the orc internment camps and rebuild the blasted kingdom of Stormwind. Seeing little personal gain, Gilneas built the Greymane Wall and severed ties, Stromgarde departed over territorial and prisoner quarrels, and Quel'Thalas pulled back behind its enchanted runestones. The coalition that remained under King Terenas attempted to weather the political storm, only to be utterly dismantled during the Third War when the Cult of the Damned and the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron. Arthas Menethil's betrayal tore the heart out of the kingdom, ending the golden age of the northern realm.

topic:alterac-kingdom.text: Alterac (kingdom). Alterac was one of the seven historic human kingdoms, nestled high in the rugged Alterac Mountains. During the Second War, its ruler, King Aiden Perenolde, made a treacherous pact with the Old Horde to spare his realm, leading to the kingdom's military downfall and total collapse. Today, its ruined capital lies abandoned in the snow, while dispossessed nobles and outlaws wage a guerrilla war under the banner of the Syndicate. Alterac arose thousands of years ago as an Arathorian city-state following the Troll Wars. Settlers capitalized on strategic mountain passes and trading outposts, eventually establishing an independent realm when the empire fractured. Though rugged and mountainous, Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Historically, it fielded tough mountain fighters, but enduring border friction with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom politically isolated from its neighbors long before the Dark Portal ever opened. When Sir Anduin Lothar forged the Alliance of Lordaeron, King Aiden Perenolde joined only with deep reluctance. As Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde swept north, Perenolde concluded humanity was doomed and secretly struck a deal with the Warchief. In exchange for the safety of Alterac, Perenolde opened fortified mountain passes, conspired against Alliance forces, and even dispatched soldiers and sailors to assist the Horde's siege of Lordaeron. The treachery allowed the orcs to reach Capital City far ahead of schedule, shaking the Alliance to its core when the truth was laid bare. Retribution was swift. Stromgarde's forces marched into the mountains, exposing Perenolde's treason and breaking Alterac's military. King Terenas Menethil II placed the fallen nation under martial law, while arguments over who should inherit the throne paralyzed Alliance diplomats for years. Following the kingdom's collapse, King Perenolde died in disgrace. His son, Lord Aliden Perenolde, rallied the bitter, displaced nobility to form the Syndicate. Wearing the orange cloth of their fallen homeland, these bandits and mercenaries now fight ruthlessly to reclaim their ancestral holdings across Hillsbrad and Alterac.

topic:anduin-lothar.text: Anduin Lothar. Sir Anduin Lothar, known as the Lion of Stormwind, was the last descendant of the ancient Arathi bloodline and the Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron. A childhood companion of King Llane Wrynn and the Guardian Medivh, Lothar led humanity through the horrors of the First War and rallied the northern nations during the Second War before falling at Blackrock Mountain. Carrying the ancient bloodline of the Arathi kings, Lothar grew up within Stormwind's royal court alongside Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. The trio embarked on reckless excursions into the wilderness, skirmishing with Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Lothar rose rapidly through Stormwind's martial ranks, joining the King's Honor Guard and earning renown as an Armsman of the Brotherhood of the Horse. Arriving on the shores of Lordaeron, Lothar presented the grim reality of the Horde to King Terenas Menethil II. Invoking his ancestral Arathi lineage and diplomatic gravitas, he unified the human realms, Ironforge dwarves, and high elves into the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron. Named Supreme Commander of the united forces, Lothar spearheaded the campaign that pushed the Horde back south to the foot of Blackrock Mountain. There, in a fateful clash near the end of the Second War, Lothar was slain by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. His death did not shatter the Alliance; instead, it galvanized his lieutenant, Turalyon, to lead the charge that broke the Horde forever.

topic:argent-dawn.text: Argent Dawn. The Argent Dawn is a neutral, knightly order dedicated to stamping out malevolent threats across Azeroth, most notably the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Formed by survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand who rejected the fanatical zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade, they welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the cause of the Light. From their fortified sanctuary at Light's Hope Chapel to far-flung outposts across Kalimdor, they stand on the front lines against darkness. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed into ruin, the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand broke into bitter disagreement. Many survivors surrendered to grief and paranoia, morphing into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade. Yet veterans like Lord Maxwell Tyrosus recognized that their former comrades had abandoned the true tenets of the Holy Light. Refusing to succumb to madness or abandon the dead kingdom, they split away to form the Argent Dawn—an order committed to defending Azeroth alongside anyone willing to fight, whether Alliance or Horde. The Dawn's primary stronghold is Light's Hope Chapel, situated in the blighted expanse of the Eastern Plaguelands. From this consecrated bastion, the order coordinates an unending war against Kel'Thuzad's necromancers and skeletal legions. Operating forward camps at Chillwind Camp and outside the Bulwark in Tirisfal Glades, Argent officers issue enchanted commissions to adventurers, paying bounties in exchange for Scourgestones wrested from fallen undead. Despite lacking the raw manpower of the Scarlet Crusade, the Dawn holds the line through perseverance, unity, and unshakable discipline. While Lordaeron remains their principal battleground, the Argent Dawn maintains an active watch across Kalimdor and the capitals of the world. They keep diplomatic presences in Stormwind City, Darnassus, and the goblin trade town of Everlook. Farther afield, operatives like Delgren the Purifier contest demonic cults in Darkshore and Ashenvale, while scouts in Desolace and the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps investigate sinister threats involving the Shadow Council and the Twilight's Hammer cult.

topic:arthas-menethil.text: Arthas Menethil. Once the golden prince of Lordaeron and a celebrated paladin of the Silver Hand, Arthas Menethil fell from grace during the Third War while pursuing the demonic orchestrators of the plague. After claiming the cursed runeblade Frostmourne in the frozen north, he surrendered his soul, murdered his father King Terenas, and spearheaded the destruction of his own homeland as the Scourge's dark champion. Born to King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas was raised to embody the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Trained in combat by Muradin Bronzebeard and inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand under the tutelage of Uther the Lightbringer, he was revered by high and low alike as the future of humanity. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought tenaciously against Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Yet beneath his radiant exterior lay an uncompromising pride and an obsessive dread of failure.

topic:black-dragonflight.text: Black dragonflight. Once the stalwart Earth-Warders charged by the titans to safeguard Azeroth's deep subterranean realms, the black dragonflight fell to madness and treachery. Corrupted by the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods, their leader Neltharion became Deathwing, turning his brood into one of the most destructive and hated forces on the planet. Today, their surviving scions weave plots from the shadows and wage covert wars against mortal kingdoms. Long ago, the Titan Khaz'goroth bestowed his blessing upon Neltharion, creating the black dragonflight to watch over the earth, raise mountains, and guard Azeroth's deep caverns. For ages, they stood alongside the other flights as patient, unyielding guardians. Yet their intimate bond with the world's subterranean foundations proved their undoing. Dwelling within the deepest hollows, they lay dangerously close to the sunken prisons of the Old Gods. Over centuries, dark whispers eroded the noble Earth-Warder's mind, driving him to madness and twisting his entire brood into vicious instruments of ruin. During the ancient War of the Ancients, Neltharion shattered the unity of dragonkind, turning upon his kin as Deathwing the Destroyer. Ever since, the black flight has waged relentless, spiteful war against the red, blue, green, and bronze flights, who view their cruelty as an absolute profanation of life. Rather than tending the soil, black dragons now wield molten magma, black magic, and searing brimstone to scorch the lands they once nurtured, finding delight in sowing discord, misery, and endless strife across mortal realms.

topic:blackrock-clan.text: Blackrock clan. The Blackrock clan is a martial orcish clan renowned for its strict military discipline, unmatched blacksmithing, and central role in the First and Second Wars. Today, the clan is deeply fractured: while some veterans follow Thrall in the New Horde, a vicious and renegade splinter group known as the Dark Horde occupies the upper peaks of Blackrock Mountain under Rend Blackhand. Hailing from Draenor, the Blackrock clan made its name through rigid hierarchy, heavy armor, and mastery over the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they served as the brutal core of the Old Horde during the invasion of Azeroth, laying siege to Stormwind. When Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand to cleanse the Horde of Gul'dan's direct puppet mastery, leadership of both the clan and the Horde remained firmly in Blackrock hands through the grueling campaigns of the Second War. Following the Horde's catastrophic defeat at Blackrock Mountain, the clan shattered. Many warriors were rounded up and placed in Alliance internment camps, later to be liberated by Thrall and inducted into his reformed New Horde. However, unrepentant elements rallied behind Blackhand's sons, Rend and Maim. This faction retreated into the heights of Blackrock Spire, forming the hostile Dark Horde alongside remnants of the Dragonmaw and other rogue clans. Today, Rend Blackhand claims the mantle of true Warchief from his throne in Blackrock Spire. The Dark Horde maintains an uneasy and treacherous truce with the Dark Iron dwarves who lurk in the molten depths below, all while waging war against both the Alliance and Thrall's Horde. Uncompromising, demon-tainted remnants of the clan have also been spotted lingering in Lordaeron, seeking to revive dark sacrificial rituals.

topic:bronzebeard-clan.text: Bronzebeard clan. The Bronzebeard clan is the ruling dwarven royal line and dominant population of Ironforge. Following their victory in the ancient War of the Three Hammers, they forged strong ties with humanity and the gnomes, standing today under King Magni Bronzebeard as a cornerstone of the Alliance. Long ago, dwarven society in Ironforge flourished under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died of old age roughly 230 years ago, simmering rivalries erupted into civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded the traditional garrison and largest standing army within Ironforge, successfully driving both the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from under the mountain. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan mounted an assault to reconquer Khaz Modan, Madoran Bronzebeard led his clan in a decisive campaign that shattered the Dark Iron host, solidifying Bronzebeard supremacy over Ironforge. Human kingdoms first encountered the Bronzebeards nearly two millennia ago, building mutual respect through shared mastery of metalcraft, trade, and a passion for battle. When the Orcish Horde swept through the continent in the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard brought his realm into the Alliance of Lordaeron. Despite withstanding brutal sieges within their subterranean fortress, Bronzebeard engineers, gunners, and demolitionists provided pivotal firepower and arms that helped turn the tide of the war.

topic:burning-blade-clan.text: Burning Blade clan. Once an ancient orcish clan renowned for its deadly blademasters and consumed by chaotic frenzy during the early wars, the Burning Blade now largely persists as a sinister demon-worshiping cult. Its acolytes infiltrate Durotar and the Barrens under the direction of the Shadow Council. Meanwhile, a handful of honorable blademasters have forsaken its demonic corruption to serve Warchief Thrall in the New Horde. Originating in the lands of Draenor alongside clans like the Warsong, the Burning Blade were long respected for the lethal tradition of their blademasters. When they drank the blood of Mannoroth and marched through the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, however, the clan fractured mentally. By the Second War, they were scarcely an organized society, behaving instead like a berserk force of nature. Nomadic and demented, they threw themselves into battle with total disregard for survival, requiring ogres to hold them in check until unleashed. Ultimately, their numbers were battered and routed near the Dark Portal by the Alliance. Following the Second War, the surviving remnants of the Burning Blade split dramatically. A disciplined contingent of blademasters swore solemn oaths to liberate their people from demonic enslavement, pledging their blades directly to Warchief Thrall as his personal honor guard. Yet a far larger portion of the scattered clan fell entirely under the sway of the Burning Legion and the Shadow Council, morphing into a clandestine cult of warlocks, fel acolytes, and conspirators lurking throughout Kalimdor. The modern cult operates covens across Kalimdor, troubling newly arrived orcs and Darkspear trolls from their first days in the Valley of Trials. Burning Blade warlocks inhabit Thunder Ridge, and garrison a major hideout within Skull Rock near Orgrimmar's eastern gates. Their cultists rally around dark relics like the Demon Seed and harvest souls for demonic rituals, making them a primary internal menace against the fledgling Horde's stability in Durotar and the Barrens.

topic:burning-legion.text: Burning Legion. The Burning Legion is an infinite, apocalyptic host of demons led by the fallen titan Sargeras, dedicated to scouring all life from creation. Having already shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the demons remain Azeroth's most relentless nemesis, orchestrating the corruption of the orcs and the horrors of the Third War. Long ago, Sargeras stood as the champion of the titans, tasked with hunting down and imprisoning the demons that plagued the cosmos. Over countless ages of battling their evil, he grew disillusioned and concluded that creation itself was fatally flawed and must be unmade in flame. To enact his crusade, he freed the demons he had imprisoned, bending them to his will through fel magic. He augmented their chaos with the intellect of the corrupted eredar—elevating Archimonde and Kil'jaeden as his chief lieutenants—and forged an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation. Ten millennia ago, the reckless sorceries of the Highborne drew the Legion's gaze to Azeroth. Whispering through the Well of Eternity, Sargeras seduced Queen Azshara and her councilor Xavius with promises of reshaping the world into paradise. Instead, the portal unleashed commanders like Mannoroth and Archimonde alongside swarms of doomguard, felhounds, and flaming infernals. The ensuing war reduced Kalimdor's civilization to ruin before an alliance of night elves, dragonflights, and demigods collapsed the gateway. The catastrophic implosion tore the supercontinent apart in the Great Sundering, casting the ruined lands across vast new seas. Though cast back into the Twisting Nether, the Legion never abandoned Azeroth. Deciding that direct invasion invited failure, Kil'jaeden orchestrated proxy cataclysms from afar. The deceiver bound the orcs of Draenor through demonic blood pacts, sending the Horde charging through the Dark Portal to weaken mortal defenses. When that failed, the Legion forged the Lich King and unleashed the undead Scourge across Lordaeron, paving the way for Archimonde's return in the Third War. Even after Archimonde fell at Mount Hyjal, remnants of the Legion linger across Felwood, the Blasted Lands, and hidden cults throughout the world.

topic:cenarion-circle.text: Cenarion Circle. The Cenarion Circle is an ancient, independent order of druids founded by Malfurion Stormrage under the guidance of the demigod Cenarius. Operating from their sacred haven in Moonglade, they strive to maintain the balance of nature, safeguard the Emerald Dream, and mend Azeroth's blighted lands. Though historically composed of night elves, they have recently welcomed the tauren into their ranks, transcending factional divides to defend the living world. The roots of the Cenarion Circle go back thousands of years to the teachings of Cenarius, the Patron of Druids, who mentored the first mortal druid, Malfurion Stormrage. Following the Great Sundering, Malfurion bound together those who wished to study nature's ways. The order made its home in the sacred vale of Moonglade, and ever since, the Circle has held sacred vigil over Azeroth's wild places. While deeply intertwined with night elf history, the Cenarion Circle exists independently of Darnassus and the Sisterhood of Elune. Their heart remains the enchanted valley of Moonglade, centered around the peaceful town of Nighthaven, where weapons are sheathed and the wars of mortals hold no sway. This ancient neutrality was demonstrated anew following the Third War, when Malfurion befriended the tauren elder Hamuul Runetotem. Recognizing the tauren people's profound spiritual reverence for the Earth Mother, the Circle formally inducted Hamuul, reintroducing druidism to his race after thousands of years.

topic:cenarius.text: Cenarius. Cenarius, the Lord of the Forest, is the ancient demigod son of Elune and Malorne who taught the night elves the secrets of druidism. For thousands of years he served as the great patron of mortal druids and guardian of the wilderness before falling in battle during the Third War. Cenarius was born to Elune, the goddess of the moon, and the great white stag demigod Malorne. Because Cenarius was bound to the mortal world, Elune placed him in the care of Malorne, while Ysera the Dreamer embraced him as a foster mother and guided him through the infinite paths of the Emerald Dream. Blessed with powers over living wood and earth, Cenarius fathered the Keepers of the Grove and the dryads, forever tying his bloodline to the wild places of Kalimdor. Millennia ago, three youths—Malfurion Stormrage, his twin Illidan, and Tyrande Whisperwind—sought out the demigod of legend. Cenarius recognized Malfurion's exceptional heart and trained him as the first mortal druid. When Queen Azshara and her Highborne unleashed the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients, Cenarius marshaled Kalimdor's wild demigods to fight alongside mortal defenders. For ten millennia following the Great Sundering, Cenarius watched over Kalimdor and nurtured the Cenarion Circle alongside Malfurion. That vigilant watch ended during the Third War when the Warsong clan began harvesting timber in Ashenvale. Outraged by the destruction of sacred woodlands, Cenarius drove the invaders back until Grom Hellscream and his warriors partook of Mannoroth's demonic blood. Infused with demonic fury, the corrupted orcs overwhelmed the demigod and struck him down, casting a dark pall across nature's defenders.

topic:church-of-the-holy-light.text: Church of the Holy Light. The Church of the Holy Light is the dominant religious institution of humanity, guiding mortal souls through the virtues of compassion, justice, and devotion. Originally centered in the lost northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its leadership now resides within the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City following the devastation wrought by the Scourge. The Church's origins reach back over a millennium to the faith in the Holy Light that took root among the humans of Arathor, teaching them to channel sacred power to cure injuries and purge affliction. Driven by tenets of charity, righteousness, and the fundamental belief that the Light resides within all thinking beings, these teachings eventually coalesced into an organized faith. The kingdom of Lordaeron became the religious heartland of this doctrine, establishing revered sanctuaries throughout the north, including Stratholme, Andorhal, Tyr's Hand, and Light's Hope Chapel. In the First War, the Brotherhood of Northshire answered the call to battle, healing fallen defenders against the invading Orcish Horde. Because they lacked weapons or heavy armor, these frontline clerics suffered appalling casualties at the hands of the orcs. Recognizing the need for holy warriors who could both channel holy wrath and survive physical combat, Archbishop Alonsus Faol convened with Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar during the Second War to establish the Knights of the Silver Hand. Paladins and priests alike became the moral and martial bulwark of the Alliance of Lordaeron, preserving humanity from total annihilation. The Third War brought immense sorrow upon the faithful. When the Plague of Undeath crept across Lordaeron, the Church worked tirelessly to alleviate the sick and stem the contamination, only to be overwhelmed when the kingdom collapsed from within. With Lordaeron transformed into a Scourge-haunted wilderness, the seat of the Church transferred southward. Under the stewardship of Archbishop Benedictus, the clergy reconstituted its hierarchy within the newly constructed Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, offering solace, spiritual guidance, and military purpose to the battered survivors of the Alliance.

topic:cult-of-the-damned.text: Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a secretive cabal of mortal zealots, necromancers, and aristocrats devoted to the Lich King. Formed in northern Lordaeron prior to the Third War, its members poisoned the grain supplies that spawned the Scourge and engineered the downfall of humanity's greatest kingdom. Today, the surviving cultists manage the plague cauldrons and necromantic academies across the Plaguelands while actively infiltrating the cities of the living. The Cult of the Damned was forged by the exiled Archmage Kel'Thuzad after he answered the telepathic whispers of the Lich King emanating from the Frozen Throne. Returning to Lordaeron with vast wealth and forbidden dark arts, Kel'Thuzad offered two false gospels: to the desperate, impoverished lower classes, he promised social equality and liberation from misery; to the wealthy landowners, such as the noble House of Barov, he promised eternal life and an unshakeable grip upon their domains. In truth, both the destitute and the affluent were cattle intended for slaughter, bound into a death cult designed to betray their homeland from the inside. Operating in complete secrecy from the dungeons beneath Caer Darrow, the cultists honed their necrotic craft, built hulking abominations, and perfected the Plague of Undeath brought south from Northrend. They struck at Lordaeron's breadbasket, contaminating the grain stores at Andorhal. As tainted flour traveled through regular merchant routes to hearths across the Eastweald, commoners sickened and died within days, only to rise as shambling thralls under the Lich King's telepathic lash. When Prince Arthas slaughtered Kel'Thuzad in Andorhal, the cultist network was already so deeply rooted that the kingdom's doom was sealed.
