Though Arthas sailed to Northrend and ascended the Frozen Throne, the Cult of the Damned remains fully operational in northern Lordaeron under the command of the resurrected archlich Kel'Thuzad. From the shadows of Stratholme and the halls of Scholomance, living cultists perform dark rites, maintain the toxic plague cauldrons across the ruined farmsteads, and attempt to assassinate Scarlet Crusaders and Forsaken alike. Because they still breathe, these acolytes can walk unnoticed through living settlements, poisoning wells, sabotaging supply lines, and grooming new recruits to feed the Scourge machine.

topic:dark-iron-clan.text: Dark Iron clan. The Dark Iron clan is an ancient, ash-skinned dwarven faction ruling from the volcanic depths of Blackrock Mountain. Cast out of Ironforge during the War of the Three Hammers, they accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, who enslaved their empire. Today, under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, they wage shadow wars against both the Alliance and the Horde while serving their fiery elemental master. Long ago, three dwarven factions lived together in Ironforge under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died, civil war erupted. The Bronzebeards defeated both rival factions, casting out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons. Vowing vengeance, Thaurissan established a settlement in the Redridge Mountains while his sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. When both assaults failed and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on his stronghold, Thaurissan attempted to unleash an apocalyptic subterranean entity to save himself. His ritual breached the core of the world and freed Ragnaros the Firelord. The rebirth of Ragnaros violently shattered the surrounding peaks, carving out the blazing caldera of Blackrock Mountain flanked by the Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes. The sorcerer-thane perished in the cataclysm, and the surviving Dark Irons found themselves bound into perpetual servitude to the Firelord. Over centuries within the lower chambers of the mountain, they constructed the sprawling subterranean capital of Shadowforge City. Their artisans and sorcerers became masters of stone golems, dark sorceries, and steam-driven siege machinery, weaponizing the molten elements around them under the gaze of flamewakers and elemental overlords.

topic:dark-iron-dwarf.text: Dark Iron dwarf. Dark Iron dwarves are a distinct dwarven sub-race distinguished by their ashen skin, blazing red eyes, and innate affinity for fire. Banished from Ironforge following the civil War of the Three Hammers, they dwell deep within Blackrock Mountain where their society has fallen under the tyrannical rule of the Firelord, Ragnaros. Unlike their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins, Dark Iron dwarves possess dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes that burn like glowing embers. Their history fractured during the War of the Three Hammers, when their Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan sought to conquer Ironforge. Defeated and driven south into the Redridge Mountains, Thaurissan attempted to summon dark powers to avenge his losses, inadvertently releasing Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The catastrophic summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain and bound the Dark Iron race into fiery servitude. Life in the deep subterranean city of Shadowforge is brutal and unforgiving. While the Dark Irons were once merely ambitious and cunning, generations beneath Blackrock Mountain under the oppressive aura of Ragnaros have warped much of their culture into cruelty, paranoia, and tyranny. Dark Iron law knows only one sentence for infractions: trial by combat in the brutal Ring of the Law. Poisoning and political intrigue are so prevalent that Dark Iron travelers customarily pack their own rations rather than trust food from strangers. Not all Dark Iron dwarves serve Emperor Dagran Thaurissan and the cult of Ragnaros. Dissident factions have broken away to pursue their own ends. The most prominent among them is the Thorium Brotherhood, a guild of master smiths based out of Thorium Point in Searing Gorge who have defected from the main clan to hire outside adventurers against their former masters. Others operate as mercenaries, spies, or trade engineers alongside neutral organizations like the Venture Company.

topic:dark-riders.text: Dark Riders. The Dark Riders are a band of mysterious, hooded horsemen who terrorize Duskwood. Merciless hunters of magical relics, they strike from hiding and leave only slaughter in their wake. Little is known of the Dark Riders' origins. Witnesses describe hooded horsemen who speak in voices both harsh and shrill, and one was seen using a small gem to take orders from a master it called only its 'Lord'. They hunt objects of magical power across the kingdom, cutting down anyone who stands between them and their prize.

topic:darkspear-tribe.text: Darkspear tribe. The Darkspear are a tribe of jungle trolls who joined Thrall's Horde after being driven from their ancestral home in Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea. Led by Shadow Hunter Vol'jin from their temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village, they now serve as core members of the Horde across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite their alliance, they currently struggle to reclaim their new home, the Echo Isles, from the traitorous witch doctor Zalazane. Originally a smaller, less ruthless tribe within the broken Gurubashi Empire of Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear endured centuries of warfare and famine against brutal neighbors like the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, only to face aquatic murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch. Their elder chieftain, Sen'jin, was captured and slain in dark sacrificial rites beneath the sea, but before dying he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Rescued by Thrall's passing fleet, the survivors pledged their undying loyalty to the new Horde and sailed westward to Kalimdor. Unlike their cannibalistic jungle kin, the Darkspear have adapted rapidly to the Horde's values of honor, establishing enclaves like Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, Shadowprey Village in Desolace, and Zoram'gar Outpost in Ashenvale. In Orgrimmar, they make their spiritual home within the Valley of Spirits, where shadow hunters and witch doctors commune with the loa. Though respected for their scouts, bat riders, and powerful hexes, old traditions run deep; some ancient rituals frowned upon by their allies are still practiced quietly in the dark.

topic:dragonmaw-clan.text: Dragonmaw clan. The Dragonmaw clan is an infamous orcish faction notorious for subduing and riding red dragons during the Second War. Guided by dark artifacts and foul magic, they imprisoned the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza beneath the cursed halls of Grim Batol until her liberation shattered their dominion. Today, their scattered remnants lurk in the wetlands and mountains of Khaz Modan, remaining hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde. The Dragonmaw clan hailed from Draenor and crossed the Dark Portal with the Old Horde. On Azeroth, they turned their talents to subjugating its winged terrors. Guided by whispers from the black dragon Deathwing, the clan's chieftain, Zuluhed the Whacked, recovered an ancient golden disk: the Dragon Soul. Zuluhed entrusted this relic to his greatest warlock, Nekros Skullcrusher, who tapped into its fel taint and christened it the Demon Soul. Using the artifact's agonizing power, Nekros ensnared Alexstrasza the Life-Binder herself. The Dragonmaw fortified the abandoned dwarven bastion of Grim Batol, keeping the Dragonqueen chained in darkness and forcing her red dragon brood to serve the Old Horde as aerial dreadnoughts during the Second War. The Dragonmaw reign ended when the Demon Soul was finally destroyed, freeing Alexstrasza and her flight from their psychic torment. Alexstrasza devoured Nekros Skullcrusher, and her vengeful flight laid waste to Grim Batol, breaking the clan's back. Routed and terrified, the surviving Dragonmaw scattered into the marshy bogs of the Wetlands and the jagged peaks around Grim Batol. The remnants on Azeroth live as desperate, feral renegades, fiercely guarding their dwindling encampments against dwarven patrols and vengeful dragons alike.

topic:elune.text: Elune. Elune is the revered moon goddess of Azeroth, worshipped primarily by the night elves as their benevolent protector and mother of the forest demigod Cenarius. Associated with the larger moon, the White Lady, she governs peace, healing, and lunar fury across the world. In tauren myth, she is honored as Mu'sha, the gentle left eye of the Earth Mother. Elune is one of the few true deities acknowledged across Azeroth, bound inseparably to the night sky and the larger of the world's two moons, the White Lady. While never appearing in a physical form on the world, night elven artisans portray her as a kaldorei of transcendent grace, bathed in luminescence with alabaster skin, silver hair, and eyes of pure moonlight. Ancient legends among the kaldorei claim she once rested in the depths of the Well of Eternity during the daylight hours, whispering wisdom to the early night elves. Night elven spiritual and civil life is anchored in devotion to Elune through the Sisterhood of Elune, an ancient matriarchal priesthood led by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. The Sisters invoke Elune's grace to mend lethal wounds, but they can also channel her radiant wrath to call down searing starlight upon their enemies. Her divine union with the Great White Stag, Malorne, produced Cenarius, binding Elune's heavenly mysteries directly to the druidic traditions that tend the wildlands of Kalimdor. Though renowned for peace, harmony, and tranquil restoration, Elune is not a gentle pacifist. As the Night Warrior, she acts as a fierce patron of battle who gathers the spirits of fallen heroes from the field and places them in the heavens to ride across the night as stars. Beyond the kaldorei, the nomadic tauren know her as Mu'sha, the radiant left eye of the Earth Mother, who illuminates the night and guides wandering hunters alongside her fiery twin brother, An'she the sun.

topic:emerald-dream.text: Emerald Dream. The Emerald Dream is a vast, ever-shifting spirit realm representing Azeroth in its primordial state, completely untouched by civilization. Watched over by the Dragon Aspect Ysera and her green flight, it serves as the spiritual blueprint of nature and the sacred domain where druids commune with the cycle of life. Existing outside the physical plane yet tethered to its heartbeat, the Emerald Dream reflects what Azeroth would look like had intelligent beings never cleared its forests or built cities upon its stone. Sculpted during the ancient ordering of the world, it is an ever-shifting wilderness of pristine forests, boundless plains, and primordial rivers. Time and distance hold little meaning within the Dream; days in the physical world can feel like decades in the spirit, and landmarks change shape like mist before mortal eyes. Following the ordering of the world, the titans entrusted this verdant plane to Ysera the Dreamer, the great Aspect of the green dragonflight. Charged with guiding the evolution and natural rhythm of Azeroth, Ysera dwells in an unending trance, gazing through enchanted dreamsight that perceives both the waking world and its mirrored spirit plane. The green dragons guard the rare, natural portals linking the physical plane to the Dream, maintaining eternal vigilance over the boundary between sleep and waking. To mortal druids, the Emerald Dream is the wellspring of their craft. By channeling nature magic, druids can project their spirits into the Dream, leaving their corporeal bodies resting safely in barrow dens for years or even centuries. In this untamed realm, they commune with ancient nature spirits and the Wild Gods, gaining profound insight into the Great Cycle of life and death. Skilled walkers of the Dream learn to transcend physical laws while in their dreamforms, traversing vast distances or slipping through solid barriers at will.

topic:explorers-league.text: Explorers' League. The Explorers' League is a renowned dwarven archaeological guild headquartered in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Founded under King Magni Bronzebeard and led by his wandering brother Brann, the League seeks to uncover the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Their expansive digs span across Azeroth, uncovering ancient titan ruins while frequently igniting regional conflicts. For centuries, the dwarves of Khaz Modan focused their formidable energies on mining, stonework, and engineering. That focus changed drastically when ancient ruins were unearthed, hinting at a forgotten legacy connecting dwarves to mythical titan creators. Eager to solve the mystery of his people's beginnings, King Magni Bronzebeard decreed that dwarven industry pivot heavily toward archaeology. Magni, alongside his brother Brann, established the Explorers' Guild—now widely known as the Explorers' League—to scour the world for relics, forgotten cities, and traces of their ancient ancestry. The League's operations are directed from the cavernous Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, oversaw on a day-to-day administrative level by High Explorer Muninn Magellas while Brann Bronzebeard explores distant reaches. Across Khaz Modan and beyond, prospectors manage extensive digsites. Sites like Ironband's Excavation in Loch Modan and Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands uncover immense fossil records and ancient architecture. However, prospectors often find themselves under siege by displaced wildlife, troggs, and rival factions interested in subterranean relics. The League's aggressive expeditions have sparked fierce resistance outside dwarven homelands. In Kalimdor, League operations such as the Bael Modan dig in the southern Barrens drove out the native Stonespire tauren through heavy industrial blasting, stirring vengeance and angering local earth spirits. In the arid Badlands, League prospectors clash openly with the Dark Iron clan over the vast titan vaults of Uldaman.

topic:first-war.text: First War. The First War was the devastating five-year conflict in which the Orcish Horde emerged through the Dark Portal and completely destroyed the human Kingdom of Stormwind. Orchestrated behind the scenes by the demon-possessed Guardian Medivh and the warlock Gul'dan, it concluded with the assassination of King Llane Wrynn I and the flight of human survivors north to Lordaeron. Before the war, the Kingdom of Stormwind enjoyed long years of peace following the Gnoll War, guarded by its Knights and the Clerics of Northshire Abbey. That stability shattered when the Guardian Medivh, secretly possessed by the demon lord Sargeras, contacted the orc warlock Gul'dan on Draenor. Together, they forged the Dark Portal in the swampy Black Morass. Driven by demon blood and the slow death of their homeworld, the Orcish Horde crossed into Azeroth in force. Early rumors dismissed the invaders as vengeful spirits or strange offshoots of trolls, but Sir Anduin Lothar's scouting patrols quickly confirmed the arrival of a disciplined, bloodthirsty army. Led openly by Warchief Blackhand and manipulated from the shadows by Gul'dan's Shadow Council, the Horde overran the southern reaches of the kingdom. While an attempt by the orcs to push into Stranglethorn Vale against the Gurubashi trolls failed, their campaign across human territory proved catastrophic. The Horde conquered outward until only Elwynn Forest remained under human control. Blackhand launched a first direct assault on Stormwind City, but Sir Anduin Lothar repelled the invasion with a brilliant, surprise flanking counterattack by sea, temporarily saving the capital from annihilation.

topic:forsaken.text: Forsaken. The Forsaken are a free-willed faction of intelligent undead who broke away from the Scourge following the Third War. Led by the Banshee Queen Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, they dwell within the subterranean Undercity carved beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's capital. Though deeply distrusted across Azeroth, they maintain a tenuous alliance of convenience with the Horde. When the Lich King's grip over his northern armies slipped after the Third War, thousands of undead in the blighted ruins of Lordaeron suddenly regained their sapience and memories. Horrified by the butchery they had been forced to carry out while enslaved to his will, these former citizens found themselves reviled and hunted by the living. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the fallen ranger-general of Quel'Thalas who had been transformed into an unholy banshee, rallied these adrift spirits, claimed the catacombs beneath Capital City, and dubbed her new nation the Forsaken. Hemmed in by relentless enemies—chief among them the fanatic Scarlet Crusade and the Scourge—Sylvanas dispatched emissaries seeking allies. Across the Great Sea in Kalimdor, tauren elders counseled compassion, believing the cursed people might yet find redemption or a cure through the earth. Despite Warchief Thrall's misgivings, the Horde admitted the Forsaken, gaining a vital northern foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms.

topic:frostmane-tribe.text: Frostmane tribe. Across Dun Morogh’s frigid peaks, the Frostmane tribe fights to reclaim its home. These ice trolls are native to the mountains, but dwarves drove them into caves and remote ridges centuries ago. From there, the Frostmane wage a guerrilla war against the dwarves. Long before the Bronzebeard clan united under Ironforge, the Frostmane trolls ruled across Dun Morogh’s snowbound reaches. The rise and spread of the dwarven kingdom crushed their realm, forcing survivors to retreat into caves and along frozen ridges and crags. That defeat bred a bitter hatred passed down through generations. To the Frostmane, every mountaineer, traveler, and homestead is an invader to drive out or slaughter. For decades, the Ironforge Senate saw the Frostmane as little more than a nuisance in the hills. Then the trogg menace emerged deep beneath Dun Morogh, throwing dwarven defenses into disarray. With the mountaineers overwhelmed and dwarven forces fighting Alliance wars abroad, the Frostmane seized their chance. From strongholds such as Frostmane Hold and Shimmer Ridge, they launched renewed, violent raids to reclaim their ancient lands.

topic:gnoll.text: Gnoll. Gnolls are a savage, hyena-like race of humanoid scavengers and raiders found scattered across both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Renowned for their vicious infighting, brutal strength, and animal cunning, they survive by pillaging settlements, butchering wildlife, and ambushing unwary travelers. Left unchecked, their sprawling packs and warlords pose a constant threat to frontier hamlets and trade roads alike. Standing slightly shorter than the average human but possessing explosive physical power, gnolls are bipedal hyena-kin known for their spiky teeth, thick pelts, and distinct barking laugh. While fully capable of walking upright, they often drop to all fours to lope swiftly through brush or track prey by scent. Gnoll culture values raw physical dominance above all else. They organize into fractious packs led by the strongest, cruelest alpha, only yielding when battered into submission by a superior force. Though usually fractured by petty squabbles, united gnolls once waged open war on the kingdom of Stormwind. Stormwind's armies prevailed in that Gnoll War, and the kingdom enjoyed a lasting peace afterward until the orcs came through the Dark Portal. Gnoll menace is not limited to the human south. In northern Lordaeron, the Scourge necromancer Thule Ravenclaw raises undead Rot Hide gnolls to dig up corpses across Tirisfal and Silverpine. Near Hillsbrad, the Mudsnout harvest foul, toxic blossoms among ruined farmsteads. Across the Great Sea in Kalimdor, the Palemane pack butchers game across Mulgore despite tauren efforts to make peace, while the Woodpaw of Feralas wage a desperate, frenzied war against encroaching silithid swarms.

topic:gnome.text: Gnome. Gnomes are a diminutive, eccentric, and astonishingly intelligent race renowned across Azeroth for their inventive engineering and mastery of the arcane. Despite their cheerful demeanor, they recently suffered a catastrophic tragedy when a subterranean trogg invasion and a disastrous defense plan irradiated their capital of Gnomeregan. Now living as refugees in Ironforge's Tinker Town, the gnomes remain staunch Alliance allies as they fight to reclaim their lost home. Small in stature but towering in intellect, gnomes approach the world with boundless curiosity and scientific ambition. While other races focus on recording histories and preserving traditions, gnomes look relentlessly forward, dedicating their lives to mechanical engineering, arcane studies, and technological innovation. Their inventions—ranging from clockwork devices and flying machines to complex subterranean trains—have shaped the modern world. Even after devastating hardships, gnomefolk maintain an irrepressible cheerfulness and an unshakable drive to rebuild and solve the impossible. The gnomes made their home in the frozen crags of Dun Morogh, and when they met the dwarves of Ironforge, the two peoples discovered an immediate kinship. Dwarven brawn and gnomish ingenuity united to carve out the marvelous subterranean techno-city of Gnomeregan in western Dun Morogh, where the gnomes are led by visionary leaders known as High Tinkers. The surviving gnomes fled their poisoned home, finding sanctuary among their dwarven cousins in Ironforge. High Tinker Mekkatorque and his people established a bustling enclave in Ironforge's Tinker Town, continuing to support the Alliance and oversee the Deeprun Tram linking Ironforge to Stormwind. From this adopted quarter, gnomish commandos and brave volunteers constantly mount expeditions into Gnomeregan's irradiated depths, striving to clear out the troggs, deal with mechanical abominations, and someday reclaim their grand city.

topic:goblin.text: Goblin. Goblins are diminutive, cunning humanoids originating from the Isle of Kezan, renowned across Azeroth for their relentless pursuit of profit, explosive engineering, and aggressive trade cartels. While most maintain a stance of strict neutrality to maximize commerce between the Alliance and Horde, mercenary and cutthroat outfits like the Venture Company and Steamwheedle Cartel leave an indelible mark on every corner of the world. Goblins hail from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas, where their society long ago divided into competing economic syndicates known as cartels. Rather than building kingdoms or armies of their own, goblin leaders channeled their ambitions into cutthroat mercantilism, volatile engineering, and industrial ventures that now reach every corner of the world. During the Second War, Trade Prince Steamwheedle allied his cartel with Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde, supplying maps, siege craft, and fleet-building expertise in exchange for Stormwind's captured plunder. Following the Horde's eventual defeat, the cartels learned that open allegiance cost them lucrative markets. In the modern era, the major cartels claim official neutrality, maintaining bustling trade havens like Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale and Gadgetzan in the Tanaris desert. Here, Alliance and Horde travelers cross paths without blades drawn—so long as port bruisers keep the peace.

topic:grimtotem-tribe.text: Grimtotem tribe. The Grimtotem tribe is an aggressive, fiercely traditionalist tauren clan that refuses to formally swear allegiance to Thrall's Horde. Distinguishable by their dark hides and fierce warpaint, they seek to purge foreign races from Kalimdor and retake ancestral lands by any means necessary. Even as their matriarch, the Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem, resides atop Thunder Bluff playing regional politics, her kin actively raid settlements across Kalimdor. Unlike their peaceful cousins who honor the Earth Mother through reverence, the Grimtotem believe Kalimdor belongs exclusively to the tauren. From youth, they are trained not in the patient harmony of the Great Hunt, but in ruthlessness, stealth, and lethal combat. They harbor immense disdain for the other races that have settled upon their ancient soils. Though Cairne Bloodhoof has welcomed them into Thunder Bluff in an effort to unite all tauren people, the Grimtotem clan stands alone as the only major tribe that has never formally joined Thrall's Horde, maintaining their own insular and violent agenda. In the wilderness far from Thunder Bluff's watchful eyes, Grimtotem hostility flares openly into violence. In Stonetalon Mountains, they butcher local settlements and threaten Horde supply outposts. Across the towering mesas of Thousand Needles, centered around Darkcloud Pinnacle, they constantly menace Freewind Post and plot to seize the canyon. Encounters in Feralas prove equally perilous: the Grimtotem attack Horde travelers, Alliance caravans, and fellow tauren without hesitation. Horde garrisons at Sun Rock Retreat and Camp Mojache regularly post bounties and dispatch warriors to cut down these violent outcasts.

topic:grommash-hellscream.text: Grommash Hellscream. After the Third War, Grommash Hellscream's people are free of the Blood Curse. Once bound to the Burning Legion by his thirst for battle, the Warsong chieftain gave his life to slay Mannoroth in Ashenvale and free the orcs. Before the Dark Portal opened, Grom Hellscream led the Warsong clan with fierce resolve. His pitch-black tattooed jaw and the deadly sweep of his two-handed axe, Gorehowl, set him apart. On Draenor, Gul'dan and the Shadow Council offered the orcs demonic strength. Grom was the first chieftain to drink the blood of the pit lord Mannoroth. The draught bound the orcs to demonic service and filled them with burning bloodlust. Many chieftains perished or lost themselves to it, but Grom kept his fierce spirit through the old Horde's horrors. He carried a quiet ache for what his people had surrendered. Left behind on Draenor during the Second War, Grom later crossed the Dark Portal and was stranded when the rift was shattered. For nearly fifteen years, he and the surviving Warsong warriors evaded the Alliance of Lordaeron. They endured the lethargy and despair that followed the fading of the demon blood. Then a young fugitive named Thrall found Grom in the wilderness, and hope returned. Grom saw Thrall's strength and noble heart, and taught him the proud heritage of their people. Together with Orgrim Doomhammer, they rallied the scattered clans, broke open the human internment camps, and began the New Horde. During the Third War, Grom's aggression rose again in Ashenvale's ancient forests. The night elves and the demigod Cenarius pressed his clan hard, and Grom drank from a fountain corrupted with Mannoroth's blood to save them. Bound again to the demon lord, he turned against his own people. Thrall and Jaina Proudmoore captured him and cleansed his spirit with ancient shamanic and arcane rites. Restored to his senses and burdened with guilt, Grom pursued Mannoroth into Demon Fall Canyon. He drove Gorehowl into the demon lord's chest, ending the demonic curse forever. Hellfire took Grom's life.

topic:harpy.text: Harpy. Harpies are predatory, avian humanoids resembling winged night elves who dwell in foul-smelling roosts across Kalimdor and the high mountain passes of Alterac. Infamous for their shrill shrieks and tempestuous elemental magic, they raid unwary travelers and blight the environments they inhabit. Night elf folklore links them to cursed betrayers of Queen Azshara, though their true origins remain uncertain. Harpies bear the upper torsos and heads of night elf women, joined to broad feathered wings and wicked talons. Despite their delicate, elven visage—which ironically grows more striking as they age—their nature is thoroughly savage. Originally roosting among the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, they have aggressively migrated across Kalimdor, terrorizing the arid canyons of Durotar, the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, and the heights of Mulgore. Unlike the wild creatures they hunt, harpies do not live in harmony with nature; they despoil surrounding flora and fauna, turning their nesting grounds into foul, fetid middens littered with the picked-clean bones of their prey. Night elf myth often claims harpies originated as treacherous handmaidens cursed by Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering, though no one can say for certain where they truly came from. Whatever their origins, harpies today operate as ruthless matriarchies, where aspiring queens must betray, slaughter, and torment rivals to maintain command. Beyond rending flesh with razor-sharp claws, harpies command dangerous wind and lightning magic, channeling shrieking gales to batter foes from above. They are deeply cunning hunters capable of spoken language, occasionally trading scavenged oddities with subterranean creatures like kobolds in exchange for bright gems and shiny trinkets. Unwary explorers are sometimes beguiled by their elven forms, but physical contact carries grave danger: a harpy's kiss is venomous, rapidly inflicting a violent, wasting fever upon those foolish enough to let their guard down.

topic:highborne.text: Highborne. The Highborne, or quel'dorei, were the aristocratic sorcerer caste of the ancient Kaldorei Empire who served Queen Azshara. Their reckless manipulation of the Well of Eternity brought the Burning Legion to Azeroth, leading to the devastating War of the Ancients and the Great Sundering. Before the Sundering, the Highborne arose as the favored upper class surrounding Queen Azshara. Claiming superiority over common kaldorei through selective bloodlines, intelligence, and opulent privilege, they strictly controlled access to the Well of Eternity. They discovered how to tap and shape its primal arcane energies, erecting magnificent cities across ancient Kalimdor. Their endless thirst for greater sorcery led them to draw deeper from the Well, turning its calm waters turbulent and dark. The ripples of arcane power created by Highborne spellcraft caught the attention of the dark titan Sargeras and the Burning Legion. Convinced by Azshara and her counselor Xavius that the demons would remake the world into an untainted paradise, the Highborne opened a massive gateway within the Well itself. This unleashed the catastrophic War of the Ancients. As demonic hordes slaughtered the populace, rebel forces rallied by Malfurion Stormrage fought to close the portal, causing the Well of Eternity to implode and tear the supercontinent apart. The Highborne fate splintered after the Sundering. Those dragged beneath the waves alongside Azshara were twisted into serpentine naga, while others fell to demonic curses and became satyrs. A faction under Dath'Remar Sunstrider aided the resistance but refused to abandon arcane magic, ultimately suffering exile across the sea to found the high elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. Today, isolated enclaves like the Shen'dralar remain cloistered in Eldre'Thalas, shunned relics of an empire that nearly destroyed Azeroth.

topic:horde.text: Horde. The Horde is a coalition of outcast nations united under Warchief Thrall to secure their mutual survival and freedom. Anchored by the shamanic bond of the orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren across Kalimdor, the faction also maintains an uneasy alliance of convenience with the Forsaken in Lordaeron. Beset by historical grievances and hostile neighbors, the Horde values strength, action, and honor over political maneuverings. The modern Horde bears little resemblance to the demonic army that marched through the Dark Portal in the First and Second Wars. After shattering the Burning Legion's grasp upon his people, Warchief Thrall led the orcs across the Great Sea to Kalimdor to build a spiritual homeland founded on ancestral traditions and honor. Along the way, Thrall forged lasting ties with Vol'jin's displaced Darkspear trolls and Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren tribes, fighting side by side to drive off centaur and demonic incursions during the Third War. In Kalimdor, the orcs carved out the nation of Durotar and built the fortress capital of Orgrimmar, offering the Darkspear refuge upon the nearby Echo Isles. Just south, in the lush plains of Mulgore, the nomadic tauren unified around Thunder Bluff under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Sharing shamanic reverence, a deep bond with nature, and mutual survival needs, these three races view each other not as tactical assets, but as an enduring family bound by spilled blood and spiritual respect. Across the sea in the ruined lands of Lordaeron, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner led the free-willed Forsaken out of the Scourge's grasp. Desperate for allies against surviving human factions and remnants of the Scourge, Sylvanas sought a place within the Horde. Tauren elders argued the undead might yet be redeemed, and Thrall admitted the Forsaken into the Horde, establishing a vital military outpost in the Eastern Kingdoms despite persistent misgivings among Kalimdor's ranks. Despite Thrall's hopes to build an enduring peace with the Alliance, the legacy of the Old Horde casts an inescapable shadow. To human and dwarven eyes, orcs remain bloodthirsty invaders, and undead can never be trusted. Clashes over vital lumber in Ashenvale and skirmishes along territorial borders have plunged both factions into a tense, fragile cold war. Thrall actively directs campaigns against demon cults like the Burning Blade to prove the Horde has severed ties with the Legion, but deep-seated hatred threatens to reignite all-out war at any spark.

topic:juggernaught.text: Juggernaught. A Juggernaught is an enormous, heavily armored battleship bristling with heavy naval cannons. Built with ogre help to serve as the iron core of the Old Horde's fleet during the Second War, these floating fortresses were built to pulverize coastal strongholds and trade routes. Reports of a great vessel beneath Westfall draw attention to the hidden workings of the Defias Brotherhood. Orcs were not traditionally a seafaring culture, so when the Horde required a fleet capable of crossing the Great Sea and contesting the Alliance's naval superiority during the Second War, they relied heavily on ogre ingenuity. The resulting craft—the ogre juggernaught—became the backbone of the Horde armada. Though vastly slower and less nimble than swift troll destroyers, these behemoths carried immense plating and devastating broadside batteries that could shatter Alliance hulls and smash shore fortifications to rubble.

topic:knights-of-the-silver-hand.text: Knights of the Silver Hand. The Knights of the Silver Hand are the legendary order of holy paladins founded after the First War to combine martial combat with the healing and smiting power of the Holy Light. Though their original northern chapter was broken during the fall of Lordaeron, surviving knights carry on their sacred vows in Stormwind and Ironforge, while scattered remnants battle the undead in the northern Plaguelands. Following the destruction of Stormwind during the First War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol recognized a dire flaw in the Alliance's defenses: the clerics of Northshire were devoted and skilled healers, but they lacked martial training and fell easily on the front lines. To ensure holy warriors could endure the brutal combat of the Second War, Faol and his premier student, Uther the Lightbringer, founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Faol recruited both battle-hardened knights willing to learn devotion to the Light and devout clerics willing to bear plate armor and warhammers. Led by Uther the Lightbringer, the first paladins proved instrumental to the Alliance of Lordaeron. Riding into combat, the paladins lifted the morale of weary soldiers and countered the sinister necromancy of the Horde's death knights. Throughout the war, the Silver Hand broke peasant rebellions, reclaimed Caer Darrow, and helped defend Capital City against the siege of the orcs. In the years of peace that followed, the paladins guarded Lordaeron's borders, settled civil disputes, and served as shining exemplars of honor, humility, and justice. Tragedy struck the order from within during the Third War. Prince Arthas Menethil, a decorated knight of the Silver Hand, clashed bitterly with his mentor Uther outside Stratholme and unlawfully suspended the paladins when Uther refused to butcher the infected citizenry. When Arthas later succumbed to corruption and led the Scourge against Lordaeron, Uther was slain, shattering the order's central leadership. The surviving knights in the north fractured under differing doctrines, eventually birthing the zealous Scarlet Crusade and the vigilant Argent Dawn, while the surviving chapters in Stormwind and Ironforge continue to train new paladins under the classic banner of the Silver Hand.

topic:kobold.text: Kobold. Kobolds are diminutive, rat-like subterranean humanoids found scuttling through mines and caverns across Azeroth. Notorious for their obsessive devotion to the tallow candles strapped to their heads, they are individually cowardly but dangerous in swarms, fiercely defending their dig sites against any who threaten their light. Standing barely four feet tall, kobolds are filthy, subterranean scavengers who spend their lives delving into the earth. Though they possess low-light vision, the deepest shafts are pitch-black, compelling every kobold to affix a crude candle to their head. While cowardly when cornered alone, kobolds breed in massive numbers and work with relentless energy. When agitated, their rat-like tails whip violently, and they overwhelm intruders in frantic mobs, beating foes to death with heavy iron mining picks. To a kobold, a candle is far more than a light source; it is an existential shield. They harbor a deep, primal terror of the pitch-black tunnels, believing that the unlit darkness will actively consume them. Across the Eastern Kingdoms, kobolds frequently overrun commercial mines. In Elwynn Forest, a clan displaced from the Redridge Mountains seized the Echo Ridge, Fargodeep, and Jasperlode mines, driven in part by Riverpaw gnolls and the Defias Brotherhood. In Loch Modan, the Tunnel Rat clan seized the Silver Stream Mine from the dwarven Miners' League. Even on Kalimdor, kobolds plague industrial digs, laboring for the Venture Company in Stonetalon or uncovering strange minerals in Thousand Needles.

topic:kolkar-clan.text: Kolkar clan. The Kolkar are an aggressive clan of centaur native to central Kalimdor, claiming descent from the legendary first Khan, Kolk. They maintain strongholds in Desolace and across the Barrens, frequently raiding Horde settlements and fighting anyone who crosses their path. The Kolkar take their name from Khan Kolk, the legendary first centaur khan born from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. Driven by a deep hatred for other races and their fellow centaur clans alike, the Kolkar distinguish themselves by their red markings and an absolute refusal to form alliances. Historically based out of their ancient village in eastern Desolace, the restless spirit of Khan Kolk still wanders the subterranean depths of their ancestral lands. For generations, the nomadic tauren endured brutal raids from the Kolkar as they traversed the arid Barrens. When the orcs arrived on Kalimdor during the Third War, Thrall allied with Cairne Bloodhoof to push the marauding centaur back and escort the tauren to safety in Mulgore. Defeat did not break the clan; instead, it fueled a lingering blood feud. The Kolkar entrenched themselves around all three vital water sources in the Barrens: the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis. Emboldened by their fortified positions across the savanna, the Kolkar have pushed eastward past the Southfury River into Durotar itself. From Kolkar Crag in the south, raiding parties plot assaults against Sen'jin Village, the Valley of Trials, and the paths approaching Orgrimmar. While senior Horde leadership focuses on larger regional threats, young recruits are dispatched to cull the centaur advance before their raiding parties can strike the nascent orc capital.

topic:kul-tiras.text: Kul Tiras. Kul Tiras is an insular maritime human kingdom situated on an island archipelago in the Great Sea, west of Dun Morogh and Baradin Bay. Renowned for possessing the mightiest navy in Azeroth, it served as a cornerstone of the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. Following the fracturing of the old Alliance and tragic losses in Kalimdor, the island realm has largely receded into isolated waters. Kul Tiras blossomed into an unmatched seafaring power, sustained by an industrious merchant marine, rich fishing grounds, and a naval armada without peer in human history. When the Orcish Horde swept through the Eastern Kingdoms, Kul Tiras answered the call of King Terenas Menethil II and committed its armada to the Alliance of Lordaeron. Lord Admiral Daelin Proudmoore commanded the naval forces of humanity, waging bloody warfare across the open ocean to sever the Horde's sea lanes and protect coastal shores. However, following the war's conclusion and the eventual splintering of the northern kingdoms, Kul Tiras pulled back its fleets, withdrawing into heavy coastal defense and quiet insularity.

topic:lordaeron.text: Lordaeron. Lordaeron is the great northern subcontinent of the Eastern Kingdoms, once the glorious heart of human civilization and the Alliance. Following the devastation of the Third War, its former kingdoms lie in ruins, contested by the undead Scourge, Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, and desperate remnants of the living. Lordaeron shares its name with the human city-state of Lordaeron, which rose in the north after the ancient Empire of Arathor and grew into the most powerful of the human kingdoms. Stretching from the rugged Arathi Highlands in the south across scenic forests and waterways up toward Quel'Thalas, the region nurtured thriving kingdoms like Lordaeron, Dalaran, Gilneas, and Alterac. It was historically celebrated for fertile farmlands in Tirisfal and Hillsbrad, mountain strongholds, and the sacred cradle of the Holy Light. During the Third War, Lordaeron became ground zero for the Lich King's invasion. Through tainted grain, the Cult of the Damned transformed countless northern citizens into mindless undead monstrosities. Prince Arthas Menethil fell to darkness, returning from Northrend to slay his father, King Terenas Menethil II, and orchestrate the total slaughter of the Capital City. The thriving heartland quickly rotted into the blighted nightmare known as the Plaguelands. Today, Lordaeron is a brutal battleground defined by fractured loyalties. Beneath the ruins of the Capital City, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken have carved out the Undercity, establishing a sovereign realm of free-willed undead aligned with the Horde. To the east, the Lich King's mindless Scourge clings to corrupted keeps and strongholds. Meanwhile, human zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, surviving Alliance settlements in Hillsbrad, and wild forest trolls clash relentlessly over what remains.

topic:medivh.text: Medivh. Medivh was the last Guardian of Tirisfal, an ancient order tasked with defending Azeroth from demonic corruption. Bound from before his birth by the spirit of the Dark Titan Sargeras, he opened the Dark Portal and brought the orcish Horde into the world, setting off decades of catastrophic warfare. Medivh was born to the powerful Guardian Aegwynn and the court conjurer Nielas Aran. Centuries earlier, Aegwynn had fought the fallen Titan Sargeras in Northrend, unaware that his dark essence slipped into her body to await an heir. When Medivh reached his fourteenth birthday, the vast magical inheritance bestowed by his mother manifested in a terrifying explosion of power, plunging the boy into a decade-long coma under the watch of the clerics at Northshire Abbey. Awakening from his slumber, Medivh took residence in the isolated tower of Karazhan, serving as court magus to his childhood friend King Llane Wrynn of Stormwind. Yet the dark spirit within him slowly eroded his sanity. Seeking to unleash devastation, Medivh made contact across the stars with the orc warlock Gul'dan and the Shadow Council. Together, they channeled tremendous magic to tear open the Dark Portal, delivering the Horde upon the Eastern Kingdoms and sparking the First War. Medivh was ultimately slain in his tower by his closest friend, Anduin Lothar, and his apprentice, Khadgar.

topic:mor-ladim.text: Mor'Ladim. Mor'Ladim stalks the grounds of Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood, a vengeful skeletal warrior. He was once Morgan Ladimore, a noble knight who lost his family and was overcome by grief and madness, rising in undeath to kill those who cross his path. Before Raven Hill feared his name, Morgan Ladimore defended the helpless from Grand Hamlet, now called Darkshire. He married Lys at eighteen, and they raised three children in peace until war called him north. During the Third War, Morgan marched with Uther the Lightbringer to Lordaeron. There he witnessed the fall of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the spread of Kel'Thuzad's plague, and Uther's death. Morgan found no peace in the grave. Guilt over the innocent blood he had shed and suffocating grief stirred his corrupted remains from the earth as a hulking skeletal revenant. Travelers and the Night Watch soon learned to fear the name Mor'Ladim. With his ancestral blade Archeus, he patrols the misty graves, cutting down beasts and unwary travelers who stray near his resting place.

topic:murloc.text: Murloc. Murlocs are amphibious, bipedal humanoids famous for their gurgling battle cries, territorial coastal villages, and sudden swarming tactics. Though historically dwelling in the deep ocean, they have steadily migrated inland along the shores, lakes, and rivers of Azeroth, acting with far greater coordination and cunning than their primitive appearance suggests. Murlocs dwell in densely populated settlements along coastlines, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. Averaging roughly four feet in height, they possess bulbous, slime-coated bodies, wide mouths filled with sharp fangs, and keen vision capable of piercing pitch-black water. While individuals are rarely seen wandering far from their kin, encountering one murloc invariably means a dozen more lurk just beneath the surface. They rely on overwhelming numbers and sharp crude weaponry. Though ancient lineages suggest murlocs have existed beneath the waves since before recorded history, their widespread encroachment onto the landmasses of Lordaeron and Kalimdor is relatively recent. Historians note that this inland migration coincided suspiciously with the reemergence of the serpentine naga from the ocean depths. Some tribes appear to worship deep-sea monstrosities waiting in the oceanic fathoms. Whether fleeing darker terrors or preparing the world for their masters' awakening, their coordinated movement into freshwaters poses a rising threat. Because their garbled language sounds like nonsensical bubbling to outsiders, many dismiss murlocs as mere feral pests. However, their coordinated ambushes, mastery of earth and water magic, and communal structures hint at a sharper intellect. Renowned explorer Brann Bronzebeard has suggested that murlocs are far smarter than civilized races realize, intentionally concealing their cunning. Their impact on global history is undeniable: it was a murloc raid upon the Darkspear tribe that spurred Thrall to intervene, forging the alliance between the orcs and trolls that built the modern Horde.

topic:naga.text: Naga. The naga are a monstrous, serpentine race dwelling beneath the ocean's depths, ruled by their ancient empress, Queen Azshara. Once the Highborne elite of the Kaldorei Empire, they were warped into amphibious horrors during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Recently emerging from the dark waters, they have seized shorelines across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to reclaim their forgotten surface empire. Ten millennia ago, the Highborne nobility of the Kaldorei Empire ruled supreme from their grand capital of Zin-Azshari. Consumed by an obsession with arcane power, Queen Azshara and her inner court tapped the Well of Eternity to draw the gaze of the Dark Titan Sargeras, inviting the catastrophic invasion known as the War of the Ancients. When the Well of Eternity collapsed into ruin, triggering the Great Sundering, the palace slipped into the crushing abyss. Facing utter annihilation, Azshara bargained with the malevolent Old Gods deep below. In exchange for survival, she and her followers were transformed into cold, scaly, serpentine beings bound to the deeps. Submerged at the seafloor beneath the swirling fury of the Maelstrom, the survivors erected the aquatic empire of Nazjatar. Nursing a ten-thousand-year grudge against the surface world, the naga preserved their Highborne arrogance while mutating into distinct casts: hulking, brute-like warriors and multi-armed, spell-weaving sea witches. Under Azshara's unyielding gaze, they perfected their mastery over sea creatures, storm magic, and frost sorcery, slowly rebuilding their strength in wait for an opportunity to strike back against land-dwellers. The naga broke their ten-thousand-year silence during the Third War. Thrall's Horde first encountered the sea witch Zar'jira in the Great Sea, while Lady Vashj answered the summons of Illidan Stormrage, marching naga forces across the ruins of Dalaran. Across the world today, naga encampments encroach aggressively upon coastlines in Azshara, Darkshore, Ashenvale, Desolace, Feralas, Dustwallow Marsh, Hillsbrad, Arathi, and Stranglethorn. Driven by ancient contempt and whispers of the Old Gods, they forge quiet alliances with the Twilight's Hammer and savage satyrs to claim what was once theirs.

topic:night-elf.text: Night elf. The night elves, or kaldorei, are an ancient and reclusive race native to the forests of northern Kalimdor. Once the masters of a sprawling magical empire, they abandoned arcane magic following the catastrophic War of the Ancients and turned to the worship of Elune and the path of druidism. In the wake of the Third War, having sacrificed their immortality to stop the Burning Legion, they joined the Alliance to defend their ancestral lands from Horde encroachment. Millennia ago, an inquisitive nocturnal tribe gathered around the shores of the Well of Eternity, a vast font of raw arcane energy. Over generations, the Well's cosmic magic transformed them into tall, violet-skinned, long-lived beings who called themselves the kaldorei—'children of the stars.' Guiding their early society were the moon goddess Elune and the forest demigod Cenarius, who nurtured their deep connection to the living wilds of Kalimdor. As centuries passed, the ruling caste—the Highborne, led by Queen Azshara—became obsessed with unlocking the Well's infinite arcane secrets. Their reckless use of sorcery built breathtaking wonders, but it ultimately caught the attention of the Burning Legion. The ensuing demonic invasion ended in the Great Sundering: the Well imploded, shattering ancient Kalimdor into fragmented continents and destroying Azshara's realm. Horrified by the calamity, the surviving kaldorei strictly outlawed arcane magic under penalty of death or exile. For ten thousand years, the night elves retreated into seclusion. Druids slumbered in the Emerald Dream to heal the world while the Priestesses of Elune and Sentinels stood guard over Kalimdor's woodlands beneath the World Tree Nordrassil. This isolation ended during the Third War when the Legion returned to attack Mount Hyjal. The kaldorei sacrificed their immortality to defeat Archimonde. Now, led by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, the night elves dwell in their young World Tree, Teldrassil, and fight alongside the Alliance to safeguard Ashenvale.

topic:night-watch.text: Night Watch. In Duskwood, the Night Watch holds Darkshire and the forest roads against rising threats. Abandoned by Stormwind's House of Nobles, the local volunteers face undead, feral worgen, and necromancy with Commander Althea Ebonlocke at their head. They depend heavily on travelers to defend their home. Stormwind withdrew its royal garrison after foul magic consumed the Grand Hamlet and changed the forest into Duskwood. King Varian Wrynn had disappeared, and the troops were recalled to the capital. Left without royal soldiers or supplies, Darkshire's townsfolk formed the Night Watch. They swore to defend Darkshire's borders against the horrors creeping out of the woods. From its headquarters in Darkshire, the Night Watch patrols roads buried in unnatural mist. Skeletal fiends and ghouls emerge from Raven Hill and Tranquil Gardens cemeteries, while feral worgen prowl Roland's Doom and Brightwood Grove. The militia is badly outnumbered and short of resources, and many of its finest defenders have fallen to threats such as Mor'Ladim, the wandering skeletal warrior. Commander Althea Ebonlocke, daughter of Darkshire's mayor, directs the defense with grim pragmatism. With no veteran reinforcements, she enlists capable travelers to thin skeletal legions, cull starving wolf packs, and investigate mysterious local murders. The Night Watch is the last barrier protecting human life in the region. If its lines break, Darkshire will fall into shadow.

topic:nordrassil.text: Nordrassil. Nordrassil, the 'Crown of the Heavens,' is the original World Tree planted atop Mount Hyjal to shield the second Well of Eternity. Blessed by the Great Dragon Aspects, it granted the night elves ageless immortality and a deep connection to the Emerald Dream for ten thousand years. Its sacrifice during the climax of the Third War broke Archimonde's assault, leaving the tree wounded and the night elves mortal. Ten thousand years ago, in the ashes of the Great Sundering, Illidan Stormrage cast vials of the original Well of Eternity into a mountaintop lake atop Mount Hyjal, birthing a new font of arcane power. To prevent this raw magic from corrupting the world or drawing the Burning Legion anew, the Dragon Aspect Alexstrasza planted an acorn from the Mother Tree, G'Hanir, directly over the waters. From it grew Nordrassil. The roots spread deep beneath Azeroth, sealing the Well's volatile energies and distributing gentle, life-giving vigor across the continents. Nordrassil became the spiritual and cultural heart of night elf civilization through the blessings of three Great Dragon Aspects. Alexstrasza imbued the tree with peerless vigor, extending vitality to the kaldorei. Ysera bound the tree to the Emerald Dream, allowing night elven druids to enter her slumbering realm with effortless clarity. Crucially, Nozdormu the Timeless One cast his blessing across its boughs: as long as the colossal tree stood, the night elves would never age or fall prey to natural disease, gifting an entire race with enduring immortality. Nordrassil's tranquility ended with the Third War, when the demon lord Archimonde marched upon Mount Hyjal to tear the tree apart and claim the Well's infinite power. With mortal defenders pushed to the brink, Malfurion Stormrage made the ultimate choice. Sounding the Horn of Cenarius, he called upon thousands of nature spirits and unleashed the stored enchantments within Nordrassil itself. The ensuing cataclysmic blast obliterated Archimonde and decimated the Legion. Though Nordrassil survived to heal slowly, its enchantments shattered—stripping the night elves of their beloved immortality.

topic:old-horde.text: Old Horde. The Old Horde was the blood-crazed coalition of orcish clans manipulated by demonic power into conquering Draenor and invading Azeroth. Led first by Blackhand and later by Orgrim Doomhammer, its path of destruction shaped the First and Second Wars until its decisive defeat by the Alliance of Lordaeron. Today, Thrall's New Horde seeks to overcome that dark legacy, while isolated remnants like the Dark Horde still cling to its bloody past. Before it crossed into Azeroth, the Horde was forged on Draenor through demonic manipulation. The demon lord Kil'jaeden used the warlock Gul'dan and the elder shaman Ner'zhul to corrupt the proud, spiritual orc clans. As elemental spirits abandoned the warring orcs, shamanistic traditions were cast aside for warlock magic. Sealed by the consumption of the blood of Mannoroth, the clans surrendered to bloodlust, slaughtering the draenei and draining their homeland of life. With Draenor's lands withering away and resources exhausted, the warlock Gul'dan and the possessed human guardian Medivh opened the Dark Portal into Azeroth. The Horde poured through, igniting the First War against the Kingdom of Stormwind. Under Warchief Blackhand—and the covert strings of Gul'dan's Shadow Council—the Horde battered the southern realm. Toward the war's conclusion, Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand and purged the Shadow Council, taking command of the Horde and razing Stormwind to the ground. Orgrim Doomhammer drove the Horde north across the seas into the Second War, forging alliances with forest trolls and goblin mercenaries. However, at the height of the siege of Lordaeron, Gul'dan deserted the war effort with his loyalists to seek the Tomb of Sargeras. Fractured and reeling from the betrayal, the Horde was pushed back to Blackrock Mountain and crushed by the Alliance of Lordaeron. Defeated, their portal destroyed, surviving orcs were herded into internment camps, afflicted with lethargy as the demonic blood haze faded.

topic:orc.text: Orc. Originally a shamanistic clan people hailing from the alien world of Draenor, the orcs were deceived and corrupted into a bloodthirsty conquering force by the demonic Burning Legion. After invading Azeroth and suffering eventual defeat and internment, they were rallied by Warchief Thrall to reclaim their spiritual heritage. In this new era, the orcs lead the Horde from their newly carved nation of Durotar, striving for honor while grappling with the lingering shadow of their demonic past. Before their fall, orcs lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers and spiritual clans across the rugged landscapes of Draenor. Their culture was grounded in ancestral reverence and deep communion with elemental spirits, guided primarily by revered shamans. Among the disparate clans were the Frostwolves, Warsongs, and Shadowmoon. Though physically formidable and deeply proud, traditional orcish society was defined by survival, honor, and harmony with the natural elements rather than mindless conquest. The fate of the orcs shattered when Kil'jaeden and the warlock Gul'dan orchestrated their corruption. Tricked into drinking the blood of the demon Mannoroth, the orcs were seized by a supernatural bloodlust. Forged into the original Horde, they nearly eradicated Draenor's draenei before pouring through the Dark Portal into Azeroth. The First and Second Wars saw human kingdoms fall and orcish armies reach Lordaeron's gates, but internal treachery and the unified Alliance of Lordaeron eventually crushed the invaders, herding survivors into miserable internment camps. Imprisonment stripped the orcs of their demonic frenzy, leaving them lethargic and broken until Thrall, an orc raised in human captivity, escaped. Reconnecting with shamanism, Thrall rallied the Frostwolf clan, freed his kin from the camps, and established a renewed Horde. Heeding prophetic warnings, he led his people across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. There, the sacrifice of Grom Hellscream finally broke Mannoroth's blood curse forever. Today, the orcs have carved out the arid realm of Durotar and built the fortress-city of Orgrimmar, striving to maintain their hard-won honor amidst renewed tensions with the Alliance.

topic:pirate.text: Pirate. Pirates and buccaneers are lawless seafaring plunderers operating across the Great Sea and coastal waters of Azeroth. Preying on Alliance, Horde, and neutral merchant vessels alike, they band together under loose flags to seize wealth, capture cargo, and control coastal coves. Their violent presence drives constant naval skirmishes from the waters of Kalimdor to the shores of the Eastern Kingdoms. Pirates—often called buccaneers, corsairs, or freebooters—are maritime raiders of nearly every race who make their living seizing ships and raiding coastal settlements. Their operations stretch far beyond simple robbery; crews regularly engage in smuggling, kidnappings, and mercenary contracts for whoever has coin. With the chaos left behind by the Third War and the collapse of northern kingdoms, naval enforcement has fractured, giving pirate factions the freedom to carve out fortified footholds on neglected islands and coastal coves. Despite common tales painting pirate life as one of romantic adventure, life aboard a buccaneer vessel is brutal and short. Crews endure squalid, rat-infested holds, harsh discipline, and the ever-present threat of scurvy, fought off only with supplies of limes. Betrayal is an everyday hazard, and captains maintain their command solely through strength and fear of punishment, which ranges from immediate execution to being marooned or fed to sharks. When battles end, buccaneers celebrate with roaring bouts of dice, song, and heavy rum. While independent crews roam every sea lane, major organizations wield enough ships to contest sovereign navies. The Southsea Freebooters harass shipping throughout the waters surrounding Kalimdor, while the notorious Bloodsail Buccaneers menace the southern seas and wage open war against the Steamwheedle Cartel in Booty Bay.

topic:plague-of-undeath.text: Plague of Undeath. The Plague of Undeath is a supernatural contagion concocted by the Lich King under the direction of the Burning Legion to scourge northern Eastern Kingdoms. Transmitted through infected grain, airborne cauldrons, and tainted waterways, the sickness rapidly kills living mortals and raises them as mind-bound thralls of the Scourge. The plague was devised by the fallen shaman Ner'zhul after he was transformed into the Lich King by Kil'jaeden. From his icy seat atop the Frozen Throne in Northrend, Ner'zhul perfected the sickness as an unholy vanguard for the Burning Legion's invasion. Testing his power on isolated human villages across Northrend, he discovered that he could snuff out life and psychically command the corpses that arose shortly after. Ner'zhul's telepathic summon reached across the Great Sea to the Kirin Tor mage Kel'Thuzad, who abandoned Dalaran to serve the entity. Kel'Thuzad organized the secretive Cult of the Damned, whose mortal infiltrators laid the groundwork to poison Lordaeron from within. The blight extends far beyond humanity. While non-human fauna generally suffer sickening fevers or rot rather than rising as undead thralls, the land itself bears the brunt of demonic and necromantic decay. Across the Plaguelands, massive plague cauldrons pump alchemical and magical vapors directly into the atmosphere, corrupting the surrounding land, where carrion grubs and colossal spore-choked mushrooms thrive. The Argent Dawn actively battles this airborne corruption by sabotaging these cauldrons, reversing their catalytic mixtures to burn the Scourge rather than feed it. Meanwhile, in the Undercity, the Royal Apothecary Society experiments tirelessly to refine a New Plague designed to slay both living foes and the undead.

topic:quilboar.text: Quilboar. Quilboar are aggressive, boar-like humanoids native to central Kalimdor, renowned for their sharp spinal quills and relentless territorial savagery. Claiming descent from the fallen demigod Agamaggan, they dwell within dense mazes of razor-sharp brambles across Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens. Their fierce struggle over water, soil, and sacred ground makes them a constant threat to travelers and Horde settlements. Quilboar revere Agamaggan, the colossal boar Ancient who perished battling the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. According to their sacred traditions, the quilboar are his mortal offspring. Where Agamaggan bled and died across central Kalimdor, enormous thorny vines erupted from the scorched earth, forming sprawling root-mazes that the quilboar treat as holy ground. His crystallized blood endures across the Barrens as crimson Blood Shards, which their geomancers dig up and revere as powerful talismans. Rather than building traditional towns of stone or timber, quilboar cultivate colossal briars that choke surrounding vegetation and render nearby ground barren. Tribes are typically guided by powerful geomancers—practitioners of an earthbound, crude shamanism who consult stones and crystals to direct the clan. These mystics call upon Agamaggan's spirit to summon spectral boars into combat. Because the arid central plains offer few oases, quilboar view water as the ultimate treasure; they stage lavish feasts when rare rains fall and defend water holes with vicious tenacity. For generations, quilboar clashed bitterly with the nomadic tauren and roaming centaur packs. When Thrall led the Orcish Horde into Kalimdor, orcs rapidly colonized Durotar and established trade routes through the Barrens, driving displaced tribes into open revolt. Quilboar war parties ambush supply wagons, are suspected of frightening tallstriders into wagon trains, and stage raids on outposts like Crossroads and Camp Taurajo. Two principal tribes dominate the open plains: the Razormane and the Bristleback, both engaged in simultaneous feuds against the Horde and each other.

topic:ravenholdt.text: Ravenholdt. Ravenholdt, also known as the Assassin's League, is an elite guild of rogues, thieves, and killers based out of a secluded mountain manor above the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the league maintains strict neutrality from faction politics while waging an unending shadow war against their bitter rivals, the Syndicate. They test and recruit only the most cunning operatives across Azeroth, valuing peerless discipline, stealth, and lethal efficiency above all else. Tucked away in the craggy mountains connecting Hillsbrad to Alterac, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the nerve center for Azeroth's premier brotherhood of assassins. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the organization operates far beyond the jurisdiction of kings and warchiefs. Within its walls, master specialists hone every lethal art: Master Kang instructs disciples in close combat and assassination, the Thunderwood brothers brew rare and deadly poisons, and gnome craftsmen engineer intricate locks to test fledglings. To non-rogues, entering the estate is an overt flirtation with death, where an unwary step easily ends with a poisoned dagger in the ribs. For years, Ravenholdt has been locked in an escalating feud with the Syndicate, an aristocratic criminal cartel infesting Alterac and Arathi. While the League regards the Syndicate as clumsy, arrogant amateurs, their sheer numbers make them impossible to eradicate through simple slaughter. Instead, Ravenholdt employs psychological and structural disruption: by tasking contracted rogues with pickpocketing the signet emblems worn by Syndicate ringleaders, the League relies on the Syndicate's own paranoia and cutthroat hierarchy to execute disgraced members internally.

topic:razorfen.text: Razorfen. Razorfen is the collective name associated with the predominant quilboar tribe of southern Kalimdor and their sprawling thorn-choked settlements. Carved into massive briars along the southern border of the Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen encompasses the strongholds of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs. It serves as both the spiritual heart and the central bastion of quilboar power. According to legend, the colossal thorned brambles that make up the Razorfen sprouted ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. When the giant boar Ancient, Agamaggan, fell in battle against the Burning Legion, his blood seeped into the earth wherever he bled and died. From that divine sacrifice grew massive vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns, creating a natural fortress where his descendants, the quilboar, have dwelled ever since. The Razorfen tribe is among the most aggressive and entrenched of all quilboar populations. Rather than scattering into open warrens, they built complex labyrinthine communities directly within the colossal briars. From these fortresses, the tribe fiercely defends their ancestral territory against neighboring tauren tribes, Horde settlements in the Barrens, and any outsiders daring to trespass into their holy grounds.

topic:refugee.text: Refugee. Throughout the violent history of Azeroth, constant warfare has repeatedly driven civilian populations from their homes. From the exodus of Stormwind during the First War to the tragic flight from Lordaeron in the Third War, refugees remain living testaments to the devastating costs of invasion, plague, and betrayal. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War, settlements like Goldshire, Moonbrook, and Grand Hamlet burned. Following the assassination of King Llane Wrynn, Sir Anduin Lothar took command of the kingdom's remnants. He gathered surviving soldiers and desperate civilians, escorting them to the harbor as the city burned. Lothar led a massive fleet across the Great Sea to the northern shores of Lordaeron. Arriving near Southshore, the exiled survivors—including the young Prince Varian Wrynn—were granted sanctuary by King Terenas Menethil II. A generation after welcoming Stormwind's exiles, the people of Lordaeron faced ruin of their own. During the Third War, the Scourge plague and the legions of the undead systematically dismantled the kingdom. Prince Arthas Menethil slaughtered his own subjects as he swept across the realm, leaving survivors scattered and terrified. Lady Jaina Proudmoore managed to lead an expedition of refugees across the sea to Kalimdor, eventually establishing a settlement at Theramore. However, countless others remained behind in the Eastern Kingdoms, hunted relentlessly by the Scourge, the Forsaken, and monstrous horrors that arose in the ruins.

topic:riverpaw-pack.text: Riverpaw pack. The Riverpaw pack is a savage clan of gnolls inhabiting the borderlands of Elwynn Forest and Westfall. Known for their brutal raids and ruthless dominance over local kobolds, they have grown increasingly organized and brazen following the Third War. With Stormwind's military stretched thin, their presence threatens vital roads and settlements throughout the heartland. For decades, the Riverpaw clan prowled the fringes of human civilization, but their boldness has surged in recent years. In Elwynn Forest, packs led by the infamous brute Hogger prowl the southern woods around Forest's Edge and roam the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. In Westfall, they roam across the Dust Plains and along the coasts, ambushing solitary travelers and raiding homesteads. Deputy Rainer at Westbrook Garrison and Captain Danuvin at Sentinel Hill rely heavily on mercenary blades to cull their numbers, issuing standing bounties for painted armbands and severed paws. Beyond petty ambushes, the Riverpaws exhibit an unusual drive for conquest and labor. They drove a clan of kobolds out of the Redridge Mountains and forced them into the gold mines of Elwynn Forest and Westfall, working the small creatures into relentless exhaustion to extract ore. This cruel tyranny over the mines suggests the gnolls are no longer simple scavengers living hand-to-mouth, but a faction amassing wealth and consolidating strategic ground right under the crown's nose.

topic:royal-apothecary-society.text: Royal Apothecary Society. The Royal Apothecary Society is an alchemical guild established under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and based in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Composed of Forsaken researchers, its primary mission is compounding a lethal New Plague capable of eradicating the Scourge while claiming vengeance against the living. While Horde allies believe the society seeks a cure for undeath, its researchers actively harvest venoms, slimes, and toxic reagents across Azeroth to perfect weapons of mass destruction. Founded in the wake of the Forsaken's liberation, the Royal Apothecary Society serves as the scientific and alchemical arm of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. From their vats and subterranean laboratories in the Apothecarium, researchers seek to weaponize the very force that damned them. Their preeminent endeavor is the creation of a 'New Plague'—a concoction intended to eradicate the Scourge and destroy the Lich King. Unlike traditional human alchemy, which prioritizes elixirs of healing or transmutation, the Society experiments ruthlessly with foul pathogens, caustic acids, and necromantic blends, raising fallen warhorses as skeletal steeds and brewing deadlier strains of toxic blight. The reach of the Apothecary Society extends far beyond the canals of the Undercity. Field apothecaries are dispatched to remote outposts across Lordaeron and Kalimdor. In Silverpine and Hillsbrad, agents like Apothecaries Renferrel and Lydon gather local floras and distill venoms. In the arid Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim catalogs strange desert flora and creatures, while Apothecary Zamah operates beneath Thunder Bluff in the Pools of Vision. Wherever natural toxins, shifting oozes, or virulent organisms exist, the Society sends acolytes to collect samples for the Apothecarium's cauldrons.

topic:ruins-of-gilneas.text: Gilneas. Gilneas is a secluded human kingdom occupying a rugged, storm-lashed peninsula south of Silverpine Forest. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane severed ties with the outside world and locked his nation behind the colossal Greymane Wall, leaving neighboring territories abandoned and the kingdom shrouded in total isolation. Gilneas was once an assertive maritime powerhouse among the human realms, claiming lineage from the ancient empire of Arathor. King Genn Greymane participated reluctantly in the Second War, believing his kingdom could defend itself without foreign entanglements. Bitter over the loss of Gilnean lives and unwilling to help finance the internment camps for captured orcs, Greymane severed relations with the Alliance of Lordaeron. To permanently shield his realm from outside calamity, he ordered the construction of a massive stone barricade along the kingdom's northern frontier. Erecting the Greymane Wall demanded painful geopolitical compromises. The natural mountain passes used to anchor the ramparts left territories such as Ambermill and Pyrewood Village cut off on the northern side, stranded outside the gate. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron during the Third War, King Greymane refused entreaties for aid and barred the doors to human refugees, leaving the surrounding villages to face the plague and the undead alone.

topic:sargeras.text: Sargeras. Sargeras is the fallen titan and supreme creator of the Burning Legion, bent on scouring all life from the cosmos. Once the noble champion and defender of the Pantheon, his descent into madness led to the Sundering of ancient Azeroth and nearly every demonic catastrophe since. Before his fall, Sargeras was the greatest and noblest warrior among the titans. Entrusted by the Pantheon of Order to safeguard their grand creations across the Great Dark Beyond, he waged war against the chaotic demons spawned from the Twisting Nether. Incapable of conceiving pure evil, Sargeras trapped countless fiends away within a great prison. Yet eons of relentless warfare against cosmic horrors gradually wore down his altruistic spirit. Over eons of battle, Sargeras's faith in the titans' work eroded. Despairing at the evil he faced, he concluded that creation was fundamentally flawed and that order could never truly prevail. Turning his back on the Pantheon, he shattered the demons' prison, embraced the chaotic fel fire he had once fought, and marshaled the liberated demons into the unstoppable Burning Legion. Ten thousand years ago, the reckless magic of Queen Azshara and her Highborne reached across the stars, alerting Sargeras to Azeroth's existence. Whispering through the depths of the Well of Eternity, the Dark Titan seduced Azshara into opening a portal for his vanguard. Though that ancient invasion culminated in the catastrophic Sundering, Sargeras never ceased scheming to consume Azeroth—orchestrating the opening of the Dark Portal and guiding the demonic corruption of the orcish Horde.

topic:satyr.text: Satyr. Satyrs are twisted, caprine demons born from the curse of the Highborne sorcerer Xavius during the ancient War of the Ancients. Once night elves, they were warped by Sargeras into horned, hooved beasts dedicated to spreading fel corruption, tormenting their former kin, and furthering the Burning Legion's will. Across the wilds of Kalimdor, scattered satyr sects corrupt pristine woodlands, desecrate moonwells, and subvert vulnerable mortal cults. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the Highborne councilor Xavius failed to keep the Burning Legion's initial gateway stable against Malfurion Stormrage. Enraged by this blunder, Sargeras dismantled Xavius's spirit and rebuilt him as a punishment and tool: his torso retained elven features, but he gained wicked horns, taloned claws, a leonine tail, and the cloven lower body of a goat. Sent back into Zin-Azshari, Xavius gleefully passed his fel affliction to other power-hungry Highborne. Though Xavius was struck down, his demonic progeny survived, continually seeking to reproduce their kind by corrupting others. Following the Great Sundering, the surviving satyrs continued to menace the shattered night elf civilization. Over the ages they were broken and driven off, their remnants fracturing into scattered sects that linger in dark forests and ancient ruins while harboring deep hatred for their kaldorei cousins. Today, satyr clans inhabit deep woodland enclaves across Kalimdor, from Darkshore and Ashenvale to Felwood, Azshara, and Feralas. They feed directly on the land's pure magic, leeching and spoiling nature until their hooves swell with drained arcane energy. Satyrs frequently turn peaceful furbolg tribes violent, taint ancient moonwells, and serve as covert liaisons for the Shadow Council and the Burning Blade. While some work alongside Twilight's Hammer cultists or hide within ancient ruins like Dire Maul, all remain bound to the shadow of the Burning Legion.

topic:scourge.text: Scourge. The Scourge is an apocalyptic army of undead monsters, necromancers, and enslaved spirits bound to the will of the Lich King. Originally created by the Burning Legion to destabilize Azeroth ahead of the Third War, the legion of walking corpses broke free from demonic control and shattered the kingdoms of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas. Today, they wage unending war from their arctic stronghold in Northrend and their corrupt dominion over the Plaguelands. The Scourge was born as an instrument of destruction forged by the Burning Legion. The demon lords bound the spirit of the fallen orc shaman Ner'zhul to the Frozen Throne in distant Northrend, fashioning him into the Lich King. With terrifying telepathic power, he was commanded to prepare Azeroth for conquest.
