In the Third War, Magni mourned the loss of his brother Muradin in Northrend. Today, Ironforge remains one of the Alliance's fiercest bulwarks. Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan to trogg invaders and irradiation, King Magni opened Ironforge's gates to thousands of gnome refugees. Under High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, the exiles established Tinker Town, carving out a buzzing technological haven within the stone city. Coupled with the subterranean Deeprun Tram connecting Ironforge directly to Stormwind City, the dwarven stronghold has transformed into a lively crossroads of dwarven steelcraft and gnomish ingenuity.

zone:lochmodan.text: Loch Modan. The Stonewrought Dam holds Loch Modan's great lake above the Wetlands. Around Thelsamar, troggs threaten the southern valleys while kobolds work the mines and ogres hold the northeast highlands. Loch Modan's lake fills a green valley east of Dun Morogh. Pines and birches climb toward the rugged peaks, while the Stonewrought Dam spans the northern rim. The dwarven town of Thelsamar draws mountaineers, hunters, and miners. Copper and tin veins run through the surrounding hills. Broken catapults and ballistae on the lake bed recall the Second War, when the orcish Horde occupied Loch Modan before the dwarves drove them out. More recently, dwarven excavations opened underground chambers and released savage troggs. Trogg tribes, led by chieftains, have overrun the southern canyons of Stonesplinter Valley and the Valley of Kings. The Ironforge Mountaineers fight to defend the trade routes.

zone:moonglade.text: Moonglade. Moonglade is an ancient, secluded forest valley nestled high in northern Kalimdor, revered as the sacred heartland of druidism and the home of the Cenarion Circle. Sheltered beneath perpetual twilight and untouched by mortal corruption, it is a neutral haven where night elf and tauren practitioners study nature side by side. For non-druids, reaching this highland sanctuary requires braving the hazardous mountain tunnel of Timbermaw Hold. Ringed by sheer mountains north of Felwood and Winterspring, Moonglade exists in a state of eternal, serene night under the soft glow of Elune's moon. At its center lies Lake Elune'ara, a deep, tranquil body of water held sacred since the dawn of kaldorei civilization. The glade remained unmarred by the Burning Legion during both ancient invasions and the recent Third War, shielded by the vigilant demigod Cenarius and his offspring. Today, under the stewardship of Keeper Remulos, the valley serves as a peaceful redoubt where nature's balance is preserved free from factional conflict. Moonglade is the headquarters of the Cenarion Circle, founded millennia ago by Malfurion Stormrage. In the lakeside village of Nighthaven, ancient traditions guide druidic instruction. Following the Third War, the Circle took the historic step of welcoming tauren into their ranks, led by the teachings of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. In Moonglade, political loyalties to the Alliance or Horde are put aside; armed sentries enforce strict neutrality, ensuring that any violence between members meets swift justice.

zone:mulgore.text: Mulgore. Mulgore shelters the tauren in a valley beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. High natural walls surround its emerald grasslands, plateaus, and plains. After Cairne Bloodhoof joined Thrall's Horde and drove out the centaur, the united tribes made Mulgore their homeland, with Thunder Bluff as their spiritual and territorial heart. The tauren have reclaimed a home after generations on the move. Centaur warbands hunted and displaced them across the central plains until High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof met Thrall and his displaced orcs. The tauren and orcs shared ideals of honor, shamanism, and strength, and the tauren joined the new Horde. With orcish help, Cairne broke the centaur hold on the region and led his people into Mulgore. They built permanent settlements here for the first time in centuries, and raised their capital, Thunder Bluff, on the highest northern mesas. Young tauren face the Great Hunt and honor the Earthmother as they reach maturity. Their training begins at Camp Narache on the southern plateau of Red Cloud Mesa, under Chief Hawkwind. From there, they descend into the Golden Plains and Bloodhoof Village to undertake the Rites of the Earthmother. They learn to commune with ancestral spirits, forage native herbs, and respect the kodos and tallstriders whose herds sustain tauren life. Mulgore's quiet plains face threats from within and beyond its borders. Displaced quilboar have settled in Brambleblade Ravine and defiled the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks. Windfury harpies hunt wild game in the mountains, while Palemane gnolls strike from hidden caves. Goblins of the Venture Company foul sacred water wells and quarry the eastern hills. Dwarven explorers from Bael Modan have also opened the Bael'dun Digsite to unearth ancient titan artifacts, despite tauren protests.

zone:orgrimmar.text: Orgrimmar. Orgrimmar rises from the red canyons of northern Durotar as the orcs’ fortified capital and the New Horde’s heart. Trolls, tauren, and Forsaken allies also find shelter within its walls. Orgrimmar grew from the orcs’ search for a homeland after the Third War. Warchief Thrall led them to Kalimdor’s arid coasts, seeking freedom from demonic corruption and human bondage. He named the harsh land Durotar for his father and the city for his fallen mentor, Orgrim Doomhammer. Building the stronghold cost blood and sweat. With help from the tauren, Darkspear trolls, goblin engineers, and the Champion Rexxar, the Horde drove back centaur, harpies, and ferocious thunder lizards that threatened the canyons. Rugged mountains shield Orgrimmar from foreign invaders and Durotar’s violent razor-winds. The city’s natural hollows give each valley its own place in Horde life. The Valley of Strength holds the civic gatehouse, with a route deeper into the trade bazaar of The Drag. Tauren druids and shaman gather by the pools in the Valley of Wisdom. Darkspear shadow hunters and witch doctors live among the stilted pavilions of the Valley of Spirits.

zone:ragefire.text: Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm's volcanic tunnels shelter troggs and a demonic cult. The Searing Blade plots against the young Horde from caverns below the Cleft of Shadow, threatening the capital above. Ragefire troggs erupt from deep beneath Orgrimmar into a maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. As orcish builders raise their new home above, the troggs grow aggressive. Magatha Grimtotem sends Maur Grimtotem to open talks on Thunder Bluff's behalf, but the troggs slaughter the envoy. They yield only to force. A demonic cult called the Searing Blade is more dangerous than the troggs. Loyal to the Shadow Council, the fanatics plot the young Horde's ruin from caverns beside streams of magma. The warlock Jergosh the Invoker, the cunning satyr Bazzalan, and the vicious felguard Taragaman the Hungerer lead them. Taragaman presides over an altar in the lava lake.

zone:razorfenkraul.text: Razorfen Kraul. In the far south of the Barrens, quilboar tribes defend the sacred brambles of Razorfen Kraul. They revere the thickets as the resting place of their ancestor, Agamaggan, while Charlga Razorflank’s rule threatens the region. Ten thousand years ago, during the War of the Ancients, Agamaggan joined the fight against the Burning Legion. The colossal wild god was slain, but his sacrifice preserved life on Azeroth. Legends say massive thorn-covered vines sprang up wherever his blood seeped into the earth, forming thick, defensive labyrinths across the southern plains. The quilboar revere Agamaggan as their divine ancestor and claimed these thickets as holy lands. The greatest became the Razorfen.

zone:redridge.text: Redridge Mountains. Redridge Mountains face attacks from Shadowhide gnolls and Blackrock orcs of the Dark Horde. Rushing rivers cut through wooded slopes around Lake Everstill, but Lakeshire must hold the line with help from wandering mercenaries while Stormwind’s forces are tied up by strife at home. Redridge was once among the kingdom’s most peaceful regions, supplying Stormwind with timber, freshwater fish, and crops. Now Lakeshire stays fortified against aggressive incursions. Stonewatch Keep, once a proud stronghold of the kingdom, has fallen to renegade Blackrock orcs. Their control cuts off roads and threatens to overrun the eastern valleys. These peaks form part of the spine running down the subcontinent of Azeroth. Centuries ago, the range stretched much farther north. Then the Dark Iron clan summoned the Firelord Ragnaros by accident, and the earth tore open to form the fiery crater of Blackrock Mountain. The cataclysm left the northern peaks severed into the ash choked Burning Steppes. Only the southern Redridge valleys remain lush and green, exposed to attacks from the slopes above. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris plead for reinforcements, but Stormwind’s regency council has left Lakeshire to fend for itself. Desperate entreaties to Sentinel Hill and Darkshire bring no help; both settlements are crippled by crises of their own. With no reinforcements in sight, local magistrates hire any capable sellsword willing to brave the Lakeridge Highway, clear the gnoll camps, and push back the danger over Lake Everstill.

zone:riverglades.text: Riverglades. The Riverglades is a contested river valley east of the Burning Steppes and Badlands, historically claimed by the Kingdom of Stormwind. Overrun by the Old Horde during the First War and largely abandoned by the crown, the region remains a battleground as local human loyalists clash with modern Horde outposts and local wildlife. It borders Redridge Mountains to the southwest, Swamp of Sorrows to the south, and faces Tanaris across the sea. Historically part of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the Riverglades fell into ruin during the First War when the Old Horde swept through the region. Its central settlement, Sunnyglade, was sacked by the orcs, who spared its mage tower solely to study human sorcery before enslaving the surviving townsfolk. Though Stormwind soldiers mounted an effort to liberate the captives and rebuild, the kingdom eventually deemed the entire valley lost and diverted resources toward defending the core homelands. For years, the region remained largely cut off from formal crown support. Despite being left behind by Stormwind's higher leadership, the human defenders never fully surrendered their homeland. Under Knight Commander Demar Brant of the legendary Brotherhood of the Horse, the remaining loyalists hold Farholde Keep as a bastion against the wilderness and hostile invaders. Meanwhile, the modern Horde maintains their own strong presence nearby at outposts like Rog'mar and Bolder'ok, ensuring that the ancient conflict over the glades continues to smolder. Stretching along the coast of the Forbidding Sea, the Riverglades is flanked by mountainous terrain and winding waterways. Travelers on foot can cross west through Blackrock Pass to the Burning Steppes, wind southwest through Redridge Pass toward the Redridge Mountains, navigate south into the Swamp of Sorrows, or trek northwest past Twilight's Shroud into the Badlands. On the coast, Powderfuse Port provides sea passage connecting directly across the ocean to Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris.

zone:ruinsoflordaeron.text: Ruins of Lordaeron. Perched directly above the subterranean Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollow remains of humanity's once-mighty northern kingdom. Fallen to the Scourge and Prince Arthas during the Third War, the surface streets and cracked plazas now crawl with wandering monstrosities, vengeful specters, and vile experimenters. Both the Alliance and the Horde dispatch ventures into this blighted citadel to reclaim relics of the fallen past or purge the horrors lurking above the Forsaken capital. Capital City was once the crown jewel of the Eastern Kingdoms, the seat of King Terenas Menethil II and the beating heart of human civilization. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he slew his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the citizenry. Today, while the Forsaken dwell in the catacombs of the Undercity below, the surface ruins remain a forsaken twilight zone. Broken archways and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts like Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past. The dangers within the ruined grounds go beyond restless dead. Apothecaries and sinister figures like Viktor the Vile work on testing new plagues among the shadows, while twisted experiments like The Abandoned roam freely. Wrathful spirits such as Rath'mael and cursed retainers like The Baron haunt the collapsed hallways, locked in unending torment and striking out against any living or undead trespassers who cross their paths.

zone:scarlet.text: Scarlet Monastery. Perched in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery was once a peaceful sanctuary and center of learning for the Church of the Holy Light. Following the fall of Lordaeron, it was seized and heavily fortified by the Scarlet Crusade as their primary forward base in the west. Now, it stands as a sprawling stronghold divided into four wings, where fanatical zealots train, torture captives, and wage an uncompromising war against all outsiders. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a proud seat of Lordaeron's priesthood and a center for learning and enlightenment. Following the Scourge's devastation, surviving crusaders purged the halls of lingering undead and spiders, transforming the tranquil archives and courtyards into a fortified garrison. Driven by paranoia and grief, the Scarlet Crusade came to view all outsiders—living or undead, human or otherwise—as carriers of the plague who must be cleansed with fire. Past the monastery's Grand Vestibule lie four distinct quarters. The Graveyard is an unhallowed open-air terrace where fallen crusaders rise as undead abominations and torturers pry confessions from prisoners. The Library preserves precious theological texts and historical tomes, guarded by the renegade mage Arcanist Doan and his hounds. The Armory serves as a training ground where Scarlet weaponmasters like Herod drill fanatic recruits into ironclad warriors. Deepest within stands the Cathedral, the grand heart of the stronghold where the Crusade's leadership directs their crusade across the blighted north.

zone:searinggorge.text: Searing Gorge. Searing Gorge is a scorched, desolate canyon in southern Khaz Modan, bordering Blackrock Mountain to the south. Once a verdant expanse of the Redridge Mountains, it was devastated over two centuries ago by the apocalyptic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord. Today, the gorge is heavily worked by the Dark Iron clan, whose extensive slave mines in the Cauldron are closely monitored by the breakaway Thorium Brotherhood. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the territory that is now Searing Gorge was a green, rolling mountain region connected to the Redridge chain. That lush landscape ceased to exist over two hundred and thirty years ago when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, desperate to turn the tide of defeat, summoned Ragnaros from the depths beneath the world. The cataclysmic emergence of the Firelord tore the earth asunder, raised Blackrock Mountain, reduced the grand Dark Iron city of Thaurissan to smoking ruins, and burned the northern valley into a cracked expanse of ash, sulfur, and volcanic glass. Seeking raw materials to supply their war machine after the loss of their old capital, the Dark Iron dwarves seized the desolate gorge. In the center of the valley lies the Cauldron, a colossal open-pit excavation plunging deep into the stone. Within its lower recesses sits the Slag Pit, a brutal subterranean mining complex. Here, Dark Iron overseers and lumbering war golems drive captured enemies into grueling slave labor, pulling iron, mithril, and rare deposits of Dark Iron ore out of the burning rock under the constant threat of lava surges and roaming beasts. Perched on the northern crags overlooking the excavation sits Thorium Point, the fortified outpost of the Thorium Brotherhood. Having split from their kin in Blackrock Mountain, these master craftsmen offer neutral shelter to travelers willing to undermine the Dark Iron operations or supply them with rare smelting components. Access to the gorge itself is tightly restricted: the Alliance keeps the Stonewrought Pass locked down behind heavy iron gates toward Loch Modan, while Horde expeditions from nearby Kargath have cut a narrow trail through the eastern badlands to scout the region.

zone:shadowfang.text: Shadowfang Keep. In southern Silverpine, Shadowfang Keep shelters the rogue Kirin Tor wizard Archmage Arugal and the worgen he summoned. The old Silverlaine estate now holds feral beasts and the phantoms of its slaughtered defenders, while nearby Pyrewood Village remains bound to a horrifying curse. Shadowfang Keep was once Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat defended by the pious Commander Springvale. During the Third War, the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied the Kirin Tor leadership and turned to the research of the wizard Ur. He summoned extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The beasts savaged the undead, then slipped beyond mortal control and stormed southern Silverpine. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls beside the feral monsters that overran their home. Broken by guilt and madness, Arugal withdrew behind the blood-stained battlements. He called the ravenous wolf-men his beloved children and named the castle Shadowfang Keep. In its stone roosts, lupine packs and shadowy hounds thrive under trainers such as Wolf Master Nandos, watched by Arugal's massive lupine beast, Fenrus the Devourer. The curse did not halt at the walls. Nearby Pyrewood Village remains trapped in a horrifying nocturnal cycle: its people walk as men by day and hunt as ravenous worgen beneath the moon, bound to the mad archmage on the heights above.

zone:shendralas.text: Shen'dralas. Shen'dralas is a rugged, contested wilderness situated between Feralas, Mulgore, and south-eastern Desolace. Dominated by ancient night elven remnants and troubled borders, it serves as a volatile crossroads where encroaching centaur, displaced outcasts, and bristling quilboar collide. Tucked away in the heights south-east of Desolace and bordered by Mulgore and Feralas, Shen'dralas is a raw borderland far removed from major faction capitols. Its craggy passes and hidden enclaves harbor desperate groups carving out existence on the edge of wild Kalimdor. From secluded vantage points like Evenshade Overlook to lawless refuges like Outcast Hideaway, the zone is defined by those who wish to watch unseen or stay forgotten. The land bears the distinct mark of the highborne legacy that gave it its name, yet it is far from peaceful. Centaur conflict bleeds across the Magram Front, keeping old blood feuds alive and well along its borders. Meanwhile, encroaching quilboar maintain fortified redoubts such as Bristleback Retreat, turning every shadowed ravine into contested territory for any traveler passing through. Leading out north-west toward Desolace lies the Valley of Bones, a grim corridor that serves as the primary overland access route into Shen'dralas. Bleached by sun and wind, this passage stands as a harsh reminder of the violent struggles that constantly ripple through these crags.

zone:silithus.text: Silithus. Silithus is a desolate, wind-scoured desert located in the far southwestern corner of Kalimdor. Beneath its arid sands lie vast colonies of insectoid silithid and the ancient ruins of Ahn'Qiraj, sealed a millennium ago behind the formidable Scarab Wall. Today, the druids of the Cenarion Circle maintain an embattled vigil against creeping swarms, doomsday cultists. Reaching Silithus requires navigating through the primeval jungle of Un'Goro Crater and ascending a wide, rocky pass nestled in its northwestern corner. The transition is stark: lush primordial growth vanishes into a vast expanse of shifting dunes, jagged stone, and unnatural towering hives. Water is virtually nonexistent, and the winds carry the hum of insect wings and the whispering sands. The Cenarion Circle maintains Cenarion Hold near the center of the desert, serving as the sole bastion of civilization and shelter for travelers, researchers, and warriors braving the hostile wastes. A thousand years ago, this arid expanse served as the battlefield for the War of the Shifting Sands. An allied army of night elves and great dragonflights fought desperately to drive back the Qiraji, an insidious insectoid empire spawned from the ancient Aqiri civilization. When total victory proved impossible, the defenders sealed the swarms within their stronghold using the Scarab Wall and the enchanted Scarab Dais. While the monumental gates held, subterranean tunnels allowed the beast-like silithids to burrow out, establishing sprawling colonies such as Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal throughout the sands. The apocalyptic Twilight's Hammer cult has entrenched itself across several fortified outposts, summoning elemental terrors and venerating the dark power slumbering beneath Ahn'Qiraj. Cenarion Circle observers monitor the desert's spreading silithid colonies and the ancient threat behind the Scarab Wall.

zone:silverpine.text: Silverpine Forest. Silverpine Forest lies under Forsaken rule and threat from rival forces along Lordaeron's western coast. The Scourge's plague scars the woods, where worgen, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves endanger travelers. Silverpine Forest lies between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Once a lush wonder of Lordaeron, it has withered since the Third War. Ghostly fog moves among dying, silver-barked pines, and ruined farmsteads lie abandoned to the wilderness. Tirisfal Glades borders the forest to the north, and Lordamere Lake lies along its eastern shore. To the south, the Greymane Wall shuts Gilneas away from the chaos beyond. The Forsaken hold their central outpost at the Sepulcher and struggle to secure the woods from enemies on every side.

zone:stockade.text: The Stockade. The Stockade holds dangerous prisoners beneath Stormwind's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built as a high-security prison for cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, it has fallen into violent anarchy. Warden Thelwater is forced back to the entrance, seeking help to crush the riot before it reaches the capital. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched to distant fronts, the understaffed prison relied on inexperienced youths, including fourteen-year-old recruits, to keep order. They failed. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tore their wool blankets into gang scarves, and cut down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely holds the entrance, while convicts control the cells, hallways, and holding blocks.

zone:stonetalon.text: Stonetalon Mountains. In Stonetalon Mountains, sacred heights now face smoke, deforestation, and elemental ruin. Night elves and tauren revere the range, while border hostilities simmer below. Stonetalon Mountains rise from central Kalimdor beneath the Ill Winds. Moisture from the western seas brings sudden downpours and slick sandstone trails, while fierce gusts scour the lower valleys, blinding travelers with grit and hurling the careless from cliffs. Higher ridges carry evergreen forests around Stonetalon Peak. Night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades there, and watch sacred wyvern and hippogryph roosts along Mirkfallon Lake. The Venture Company has broken the range's quiet with logging camps and strip mines in Windshear Crag. The goblins, aided by the deranged leper gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, have felled old-growth timber, filled the skies with furnace smoke, and fouled mountain runoff with industrial sludge. Local shamans from Orgrimmar answered the mountain spirits' cries. Small Alliance camps nearby also resist the defilers and try to protect the highlands that remain. South lies the Charred Vale, once a blossoming wilderness and now an ash-covered wasteland filled with rogue fire elementals, black dragonspawn, and harpies. During the Third War, the Horde and Alliance forged an uneasy truce in these peaks under the mysterious Oracle's guidance. Relations have since frayed. Renegade Grimtotem tauren hold seized encampments, while Darkspear trolls in Malaka'jin clash with Alliance forces pressing out from the Barrens and Ashenvale.

zone:stormwind.text: Stormwind City. In Stormwind City, the crown rests on a young prince while King Varian is missing. Rebuilt after the First War, the city is now the heart of the Grand Alliance, though debt and political turmoil trouble its white stone districts. Stormwind was founded over a thousand years ago by descendants of the Arathi. For generations, it was a flourishing, self-sufficient realm. The Orcish Horde crossed the Dark Portal and laid waste to the southern continent, razing the capital during the First War. Survivors followed Sir Anduin Lothar north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Horde fell in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance paid to rebuild the city. The Stonemasons Guild raised New Stormwind from polished white stone, with canals running through its boroughs. Stormwind’s grand appearance hides a kingdom in debt and a court divided. The House of Nobles and the Stonemasons Guild fought over wages, and the dispute left the kingdom paralyzed by debt. The guild’s workers rioted and were driven from the city they had built. King Varian Wrynn has vanished on his way to a diplomatic summit. To keep panic at bay, the crown went to his ten-year-old son, Prince Anduin Wrynn. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon now rules as Regent and military commander, with royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor at his side. With Lordaeron overrun by the Scourge, Stormwind has become humanity’s greatest haven and the Alliance’s center. High Tinker Mekkatorque’s underground Deeprun Tram links the city directly to Ironforge, the dwarven kingdom. Across the Valley of Heroes, towering statues honor the Sons of Lothar, who vanished beyond the Dark Portal. The Cathedral of Light draws the faithful, while the Wizard’s Sanctum houses arcane study. Trade, culture, and defense across the southern seas all meet in Stormwind.

zone:stranglethorn.text: Stranglethorn Vale. Stranglethorn Vale is an untamed, dense jungle dominating the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, south of Duskwood. Once the seat of the great Gurubashi Empire, the rainforest is now strewn with crumbling troll ruins, savage beasts, and competing encampments of goblins, pirates, and soldiers. Control of the region is hotly contested by local troll tribes, the Venture Company, and rival factions carving out footholds in the heat. For millennia, the vale was governed by the mighty Gurubashi Empire from their capital city, Zul'Gurub. That dominion shattered when radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, plunging the region into a catastrophic civil war. Though the Zandalari stepped in to crush the blood god's uprising, the empire splintered beyond repair. Today, the jungle is overrun by warring successor factions—most prominently the Bloodscalp in the northwest and the Skullsplitter in the east—both zealously slaughtering outsiders to reclaim their ancestral home. Where ancient ruins fall silent, commercial greed fills the void. At the southern tip lies Booty Bay, a bustling haven carved out by the Steamwheedle Cartel and run by the Blackwater Raiders under Baron Revilgaz. The port serves as the prime hub of southern commerce and seafaring transport, though it is perpetually besieged by the rival Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored along the coast. Further inland, the Venture Company aggressively strips the jungle of timber and mines the hills for rare singing crystals. Stranglethorn Vale serves as one of the most volatile borderlands in the world. The Horde commands Grom'gol Base Camp on the western coast, tethered by goblin zeppelins to Durotar and Tirisfal Glades, while Alliance loyalists operate out of the Rebel Camp to track down the rogue Colonel Kurzen. Amid the dense foliage, the legendary hunter Hemet Nesingwary leads daring big-game expeditions, drawing wanderers into perilous encounters with prowling panthers, enormous apes, and enemy soldiers.

zone:swampofsorrows.text: Swamp of Sorrows. The Swamp of Sorrows is a murky, brackish wetland tucked between Deadwind Pass and the arid Blasted Lands. Once the northern expanse of the ancient Black Morass, its salt-crusted bogs are home to dangerous wildlife, green dragonspawn, and the ruined Temple of Atal'Hakkar sunken beneath the Pool of Tears. While the Horde maintains the fortified garrison of Stonard, the Alliance has no safe haven within the mire, leaving the wilderness largely untamed. Long before the coming of the Orcish Horde, these marshes formed the northern half of an enormous wetlands known as the Black Morass. Following the shattering of the Gurubashi Empire, the fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire to erect the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, intending to summon their bloodthirsty loa, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Sensing the catastrophe, the Aspect Ysera unleashed her powers, drowning the cursed pyramid beneath the waters of the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were stationed to vigilantly watch over the drowned structure. When the Dark Portal's cataclysm later scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands, this northern fen earned its current sorrowful name. Stonard serves as the primary civilized foothold in the swamp. Originally established during the First War alongside the now-ruined settlements of Rockard and Kyross, the outpost was rebuilt under Thrall to serve as the Horde's southernmost staging ground in the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond Stonard's palisades, strange wanderers roam the fen. A group of draenei stragglers stranded on Azeroth succumbed to homesickness and madness, degenerating into feral Lost Ones. However, a small enclave of lucid Broken exiles persists at the Harborage, wary but willing to trade peacefully with travelers. Surviving the swamp requires constant vigilance against its predatory wildlife. Deep bogs hide lunging crocolisks, venomous spiders, prowling swamp jaguars, and wandering bog beasts encrusted with marsh debris. Coastal caverns and the Misty Reed Strand crawl with vicious murlocs, while the salt-laden tide creeps continually inland, preserving rotten logs in thick briny crusts. Farther east lies Sorrowmurk, where aggressive elite dragonspawn fiercely guard the approaches to the Sunken Temple, attacking anyone who strays near their vigil.

zone:tanaris.text: Tanaris. Tanaris is a vast, sweltering desert spanning the southern reaches of Kalimdor, defined by rolling sand dunes and blistering heat. At its heart lies Gadgetzan, a neutral trading outpost operated by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Beyond the bustling settlements, the dunes conceal hostile sand trolls, dangerous silithid hives, and the hidden domain of the bronze dragonflight. Tanaris is a barren, sun-scorched wilderness. Within the walled city of Zul'Farrak, the hardened Sandfury trolls guard their isolated domain. Today, the desert floor is ruled by hyenas, basilisks, and scorpids, while subterranean tunnels snake beneath the baking earth. Because Tanaris is as close to their island homeland of Kezan as the mainland allows, the Steamwheedle Cartel has established a thriving enterprise here. From the walled oasis of Gadgetzan to the coastal docks of Steamwheedle Port, the goblins maintain strict neutrality, welcoming coin from both the Alliance and the Horde. Their peace is maintained by heavy bruiser muscle, though rogue threats like the Southsea Freebooters constantly harass shipping and dig sites along the coastline. The sands hide powers far older than mortal empires. In the eastern reaches lie the Caverns of Time, the ancestral domain of Nozdormu and his bronze dragonflight, whose drakes can occasionally be seen riding the desert thermals. To the south, massive stone gates mark the titan complex of Uldum. Yet a darker danger stirs from subterranean nests like the Gaping Chasm and the Noxious Lair, where creeping silithid swarms have begun burrowing outward across the sands.

zone:teldrassil.text: Teldrassil. Teldrassil rises from the sea off Kalimdor's northwest coast, its crown sheltering Darnassus. Druids raised the World Tree after the Third War, but its growth is troubled. You stand beneath Teldrassil's vast limbs above the Veiled Sea. Hills, rivers fed by morning dew, misty lakes, and ancient glades spread across its boughs. Darnassus, the kaldorei capital, lies at the western edge. At the base of the trunk, Rut'theran Village is the island's harbor, linked to the crown by a mystical gateway. After Nordrassil was sacrificed during the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm persuaded the Circle of Ancients to grow a replacement, hoping to restore the kaldorei's lost immortality. Nozdormu and the Dragon Aspects judged the effort hubristic and withheld their blessings. Without their warding, Teldrassil has grown with unnatural flaws.

zone:thousandneedles.text: Thousand Needles. Thousand Needles is a sprawling canyon of sheer sandstone pillars and sunbaked salt pans in southern Kalimdor. Tauren tribes cling to settlements atop towering mesas to escape aggressive centaur packs, while gnomish and goblin tinkerers run high-speed rocket cars across the dried-up seabed of the Shimmering Flats. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this territory was a lush river canyon fed by inland waterways flowing out toward the sea. The cataclysm tore the continent apart, thrusting the riverbed above the water table and altering the river's path until only dry stone and sandstone spires remained. Today, dozens of slender cylindrical columns rise from the canyon floor like a petrified forest. Tauren settled on the summits, stringing precarious rope bridges between peaks to establish villages out of reach of the hostile centaur marauders patrolling the shadow-draped canyon floor below. Atop the needle-like spires, life is far from peaceful. At Freewind Post, tauren loyal to the Horde contend not only with predatory wind serpents and wyverns from Highperch, but also with their treacherous kin: the militant Grimtotem clan entrenched at Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the defense of the plateau, seeking bold fighters to strike at Grimtotem agitators and secure the fragile bridges linking the peaks. To the north, the enormous mechanical winches of the Great Lift carry travelers down from the southern Barrens, though crossing the canyon floor remains a deadly gambit. To the southeast, the canyon walls peel back into the Shimmering Flats, an enormous, desiccated salt pan sitting below sea level. In this harsh, blinding white expanse, gnomes and goblins maintain an uneasy neutrality around the Mirage Raceway. Rival engineers Pozzik and Fizzle Brassbolts race experimental rocket cars across the hard salt to settle which race possesses technological superiority. The pit stop attracts scoundrels, swindlers like Kravel Koalbeard, and hunters hunting the hardy scorpions, turtles, and basilisks that roam the searing basin.

zone:thunderbluff.text: Thunder Bluff. Across the plains of Mulgore, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren above the grasslands. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after uniting the nomadic tribes with the New Horde. Rope bridges and wooden lifts link its mesas, while its heights offer safety from centaur marauders and shelter travelers crossing Kalimdor. For generations, the tauren wandered across Kalimdor, struggling to survive centaur attacks. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined Warchief Thrall, and together the orcs and tauren drove back the centaur and secured Mulgore’s pastures. Cairne led the allied tribes to these natural stone heights to guard their future. Thunder Bluff became their first unified, permanent home in centuries. Thunder Bluff stretches across high mesas, joined by rope bridges. The central bluffs hold the markets, bank, inn, and Wind Rider roost. Three more mesas rise beyond them. Hunter Rise serves scouts and trackers. Elder Rise is home to lorekeepers and the Cenarion Circle, led by Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. Spirit Rise is devoted to spiritual communion, with shelter for shamans and priests and the underground Pools of Vision.

zone:tirisfal.text: Tirisfal Glades. In northern Lordaeron, Tirisfal Glades is home to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken. Under blighted skies, fallen manors and dormant crypts surround their vast underground capital, the Undercity. Mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders hem them in, and the free-willed dead fight for their survival. Tirisfal was once the fertile cradle of humanity, before the Lich King's plague withered them. The sun rarely breaks through the murky gloom over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches and cold coastal hills. Old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead still stand, but most of their masters lie in mass graves or walk as restless dead. Yet a dark resilience holds on in towns like Brill and in the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life. Lady Sylvanas rules the region from beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron, yet the Forsaken are beset on all sides. Scourge thralls still infest hollows, fields and crumbling crypts, wholly bound to the frozen throne of Northrend. To the east, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has made northern Tirisfal its main bastion, centered on the Scarlet Monastery. Sworn to destroy every undead creature, its outposts and patrols wage constant guerrilla war on Forsaken scouts and civilian travelers. The story of the Glades is older than any human crown. High elven exiles once tried to settle these woods, until shadowy energies deep beneath the earth began driving them mad and they moved on north. Centuries later, the secret mortal cabal called the Council of Tirisfal chose these shadowed groves to empower its solitary Guardians, who shielded Azeroth from demons.

zone:undercity.text: Undercity. Beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City, the Undercity is the Forsaken's dark stronghold. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner took it from the Scourge and remade it into an impenetrable sanctuary. Today it is the seat of Forsaken power and the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms. Long before the plague, the catacombs, dungeons and sewers beneath the palace were already called the Undercity. They held the tombs of nobles, the poorest people of the realm and the kingdom's deepest prisons, where the former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was held before his escape. In the Third War, Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas and laid waste to the capital. The prince then set his undead servants to dig out and expand the passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule. The Scourge never saw their dark capital finished. When the Lich King's power waned after the battle of Mount Hyjal, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke free of the hive mind and took thousands of undead with her. She lured Arthas into an ambush and drove him back to Northrend. After a vicious three-way civil war against Scourge remnants, dreadlords and the human resistance, she claimed the half-finished catacombs. She named her people the Forsaken and oversaw years of labor to complete the sprawling city. The city spreads in concentric rings divided into quarters. At its heart is the Trade Quarter, linked by great lifts to the palace ruins above. Around it lie the War Quarter, the Rogues' Quarter, the Magic Quarter and the toxic Apothecarium, where the Royal Apothecary Society brews virulent plagues beside canals of green slime. Deeper still, in the Royal Quarter, the Banshee Queen holds court with her dreadlord commander, Varimathras, guarded by legions of towering abominations.

zone:ungoro.text: Un'Goro Crater. Un'Goro Crater is a sunken, primordial jungle tucked between the arid wastes of Tanaris and Silithus. Dominated by roaming dinosaurs, living elementals, and a central volcano, this lush caldera is filled with ancient Titan relics and power crystals whose origins remain a profound mystery. Sandwiched between desert expanses, Un'Goro Crater defies the geography of southern Kalimdor. Ancient night elf records detailing the War of the Shifting Sands note that the insectoid Qiraji were turned back at the crater's edges, unable to penetrate what their tongue named the 'God Lands.' Scholars theorize the caldera served as a testing ground or ancient dwelling for the Titans during the shaping of Kalimdor. Stone pylons rise along the ridges, humming with energy, while crystal formations of blue, red, green, and yellow sprout through the primeval earth. Un'Goro contains no cities, towns, or native humanoid societies. Instead, life thrives in an untamed, primeval state. Apex devilsaurs stalk the flats of Terror Run, predatory bloodpetals lash out in the marshlands, and oozes creep across the tar pits of Lakkari. At the heart of the crater looms Fire Plume Ridge, an active volcanic peak teeming with hostile fire elementals led by the entity Blazerunner. For explorers and skinners, the basin offers unmatched natural wealth—including the coveted hides of devilsaurs—provided one survives the food chain. Civilized presence in the crater is limited almost entirely to Marshal's Refuge, an elevated camp tucked into the northern cliffs. Led by Williden Marshal, an expedition of scientists, naturalists, and fortune seekers attempted to catalogue the basin's treasures only to be battered by the monstrous wildlife and driven to high ground. Today, the refuge serves as an embattled staging ground for intrepid travelers studying the crater's mysterious power crystals, mapping volcanic activity, and keeping a watchful eye on encroaching silithid swarms breaching the southern ridges.

zone:wailing.text: Wailing Caverns. Beneath the Barrens' Lushwater Oasis, the Wailing Caverns are named for the eerie whistle of trapped steam. Their maze of underground springs and fissures was meant to revive Kalimdor's sun-bleached savanna, a noble druidic effort. Now it is a warped, poisonous underworld, teeming with twisted wildlife and fallen disciples in the grip of a deep, unnatural nightmare. The night elf druid Naralex found this vast water system and devised an ambitious plan. Through a conduit into the Emerald Dream, he would draw pure primal life through the springs and turn the parched Barrens back into a thriving paradise. Deep in the caverns, anchored by his loyal acolytes, Naralex slipped into communion with the Dream. But his sleeping mind touched the Emerald Nightmare instead. The corruption seized him at once, and his conduit became a valve pouring venom and madness into the underground waters. As the Nightmare's dark energy radiated from Naralex's helpless form, his students fell to the madness. They forsook the tranquil wisdom of the Cenarion Circle and became the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Their leaders, Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn, Lord Pythas and Lord Serpentis, take reptilian forms and embrace the venomous mutation of the caverns instead of fighting it. They shield their sleeping master from any outside interference, convinced this twisted growth is nature's true evolution.

zone:westernplaguelands.text: Western Plaguelands. Once the fertile agricultural breadbasket of northern Lordaeron, the Western Plaguelands now choke beneath a toxic mist and legions of undead. While Kel'Thuzad's cauldrons ruined the region's farms and towns, the soil still clings tenaciously to life. The Argent Dawn, the Alliance, the Forsaken, and the Scarlet Crusade all wage desperate campaigns across its blighted fields. Before the Third War, this land was a verdant corridor of farms stretching east from Tirisfal Glades toward Darrowmere Lake. Hearthglen governed the northern administration from Mardenholde Keep, while the sprawling town of Andorhal orchestrated the storage and export of grain across the kingdom. That crucial agricultural role made the region Kel'Thuzad's primary target. By introducing the Plague of Undeath directly into the grain shipments at Andorhal, the Cult of the Damned turned Lordaeron's sustenance into its doom. To permanently poison the soil, the Scourge raised four massive plague cauldrons across the largest agricultural estates: Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering. Today, monstrous Cauldron Lords maintain these noxious vats, pumping venomous fog into the atmosphere. The surrounding trees twist with swollen, tumorous growths, and blighted wildlife rampages through the brush. Beneath Caer Darrow on Darrowmere Lake, Darkmaster Gandling trains necromancers within Scholomance, compounding the undead threat. Despite the omnipresence of the Scourge, several factions maintain embattled footholds. The Scarlet Crusade controls the fortress of Hearthglen in the north, purging anything they deem tainted with rabid zeal. To the south, Alliance forces stage from Chillwind Camp, while the Forsaken defend their borders at the Bulwark. Mediating and directing the fight against the undead cauldrons is the neutral Argent Dawn, which aids champions of both factions and guards Uther's Tomb—the last truly sanctified ground in the region.

zone:westfall.text: Westfall. Westfall's farms lie exposed, and the Defias Brotherhood holds much of the countryside. Once Stormwind's breadbasket, the territory now struggles without crown support or military garrisons. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind with its pastures and wheat fields. After the Second War, the kingdom's finances ran thin and its leaders neglected the territory. Stormwind sent resources elsewhere and let its garrisons go, leaving the land fallow. Now barren pastures, harsh coastal winds, rogue harvest golems, and Riverpaw gnolls make survival hard for the few homesteaders who remain. The Defias Brotherhood's arrival hastened Westfall's collapse. The bandits wear red masks and follow a leader whose name no one in the countryside knows. They made Westfall their stronghold, burning farmers' fields, salting the soil, and taking abandoned mines. From Moonbrook, a ghost town, the Brotherhood rules most of the countryside in all but name. The House of Nobles has ignored Westfall's plight, so local people have taken up their own defense. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle formed the People's Militia, a volunteer force holding the line against gnolls and bandits. Stormwind sends no formal soldiers or supplies. The Militia depends on wandering adventurers to push back the Defias and protect the farms that remain.

zone:wetlands.text: Wetlands. Fog and fighting shape life in the Wetlands, between Khaz Modan and Baradin Bay. Dwarven wars and orc invasions scarred the marsh, a rugged buffer between Ironforge and Lordaeron. Menethil Harbor keeps the Alliance connected to distant shores, amid Dragonmaw orcs, murlocs, and gnolls. Below the Stonewrought Dam, cold marshland lies under gray skies and heavy fog. Once home to thriving dwarven settlements, the Wetlands now hold sunken stone ruins, sodden bogs, and treacherous mires. You can enter by the narrow pass at Dun Algaz, coming north from Loch Modan, or cross the arches of the Thandol Span from the Arathi Highlands. Grim Batol looms over the eastern swamp, its halls once held by the Wildhammer dwarves. Defiled during the War of the Three Hammers, the stronghold became a redoubt for the Dragonmaw clan during the Second War. When the red dragonflight broke free of orcish captivity, its fiery vengeance shattered the orcish forces and laid waste to the slopes. Red wyrmkin guard the Dragonmaw Gates, while feral Dragonmaw survivors live in scattered hill camps and harass travelers across the swamp. Menethil Harbor occupies the rim of Baradin Bay, carrying Alliance trade and supplies through Khaz Modan. The port honors King Terenas Menethil II and links the Eastern Kingdoms with Kalimdor. Ships sail to Theramore Isle and, by way of Southshore, to Auberdine. Dwarven-built defenses protect the harbor, but coastal murlocs, swamp creatures, and raiders threaten vessels in the rocky channels. War reaches the Wetlands from several directions. In the north, Dark Iron dwarves led by the warlock Balgaras the Foul sabotaged the Thandol Span and seized Dun Modr, cutting off overland supply trains. Mosshide gnolls roam the central fens and threaten even Rethiel the Greenwarden, an ancient protector. Rogue orc warbands, Dark Iron infiltrators, and cursed shipwrecks keep the swamp dangerous, and its defenders must stay alert.

zone:winterspring.text: Winterspring. Winterspring is a vast, snow-covered valley nestled high along the northeastern slopes of Mount Hyjal, directly above the enchanted forests of Moonglade and Felwood. Known for its bitter cold, ancient Highborne ruins, and wandering apex predators, the region is anchored by the neutral goblin outpost of Everlook. It remains a land of fierce natural perils, sheltering remnants of the blue dragonflight while confronting demonic corruption along its southern heights. Perched thousands of feet above the surrounding wilderness, Winterspring rests beneath crisp mountain air and relentless snowstorms. Enormous exposed roots of the World Tree, Nordrassil, cut through the snowdrifts like towering wooden arches, warped and twisted during the climactic struggles of the Third War. While much of northern Kalimdor is dominated by dense woodlands and warm climates, Winterspring is a quiet land of medium alpine forests, rocky bluffs, and frozen lakes, home to formidable frostsabers, chimaeras, yetis, and thick-furred winter bears. Reaching this high plateau requires traversing the ancient carved passages of Timbermaw Hold, guarded by uncorrupted furbolgs who closely scrutinize any travelers passing from Felwood or Moonglade. At the valley's center sits Everlook, a thriving trading town operated by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Goblins welcome both Alliance and Horde adventurers with open registers, acting as an indispensable haven of engineering, trade, and warm fires against the biting mountain frost. Centuries before modern settlements arose, ancient elves built the lakeside city of Kel'Theril. After reckless Highborne sorcerers shattered the cursed Crystal of Zin-Malor, madness claimed them, leaving restless phantoms to wander the ruined pillars and frozen waters to this day. Further south rise the cavernous heights of Mazthoril, the traditional Kalimdor stronghold of the blue dragonflight. Here, the brood of the Spell-Weaver Malygos, overseen by the matron protector Haleh, watches over arcane currents and contests local threats. The serenity of Winterspring is sharply broken along its southernmost border at Darkwhisper Gorge. There, elite demonic forces, remnant legions from the Third War, crawl along jagged canyons blocking the high approaches toward the summit of Mount Hyjal. Meanwhile, the native Winterfall furbolgs have succumbed to foul corruptions, prompting independent researchers like Donova Snowden to investigate the encroaching taint before the entire valley's wildlife is consumed.

zone:zephras.text: Zephras Isle. Zephras Isle is a flying island suspended within Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air. It serves as the ancestral starting home of the Skyborne, whose society now faces an existential crisis as the island's sustaining magic steadily erodes. With contact severed from neighboring sky-realms, its inhabitants struggle against elemental collapse and arriving refugees. Zephras Isle is an isolated landmass adrift in the endless winds of Skywall. For generations, the Skyborne lived here alongside native air elementals who helped preserve the magical currents holding the isle aloft. However, several centuries ago, those elemental stewards vanished entirely. Deprived of their presence and guardianship, the latent enchantments upholding the land have slowly begun to fail, causing Zephras to slowly fracture and destabilize. Zephras was not the only sanctuary inhabited by the Skyborne within the Elemental Plane. Sister islands known as Anvilas and Siroccas also drifted across Skywall, but communications between them ceased after the elementals vanished. In recent times, refugees from these crumbling neighboring landmasses have managed to reach Zephras seeking safety, bearing grim tidings that the other islands are disintegrating outright beneath their feet. With their own landmass in slow decay, the Skyborne of Zephras have begun looking beyond the boundaries of Skywall toward Azeroth. From the skydocks of Valanaar, airships now venture forth to establish rare lifelines to the mortal realm. These voyages connect the airy domain directly to points on Azeroth, including the outskirts of Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains and the Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.
